source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Inline Flag

requirements.text: The `inline` flag on a request indicates that the response MUST include the contents of all specified inlineable attributes. Inlineable attributes include:

review.note: The server tests exercise each listed inlineable category: Registry configuration, Registry collections, Resource and Version documents, and Resource metadata. Producer and client behavior are not qualified by these tests.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Inline Flag

requirements.text: Specifying the name of a non-inlineable attribute MUST generate an error ([inline_noninlineable](#inline_noninlineable)).

review.note: The HTTP contract returns inline_noninlineable for the known non-inlineable name `name`. The separate bad_inline clause also names non-inlineable values, so this evidence is qualified to the specific server error requirement; producer behavior is not established.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Inline Flag

requirements.text: While the `<RESOURCE>` and `<RESOURCE>base64` attributes are defined as two separate attributes, they are technically two separate "views" of the same underlying data. As such, the usage of each will be based on the content type of the Resource, and specifying `<RESOURCE>` in the `inline` flag value MUST be interpreted as a request for the appropriate attribute. In other words, `<RESOURCE>base64` is not a valid `inline` value.

review.note: Inlining the Resource singular chooses the appropriate JSON/string/base64 representation; explicitly requesting the base64 field as an inline selector is invalid. Direct producer vectors verify both field exclusivity and early rejection without acquiring a source.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Inline Flag

requirements.text: The value of the `inline` flag is a list of `<PATH>` values where each is a string indicating which inlineable attribute to show in the response. References to nested attributes are represented using an [xRegistry dot (`.`) notation](#xregistry-dot--notation) where the xRegistry collection names along the hierarchy are concatenated. For example: `endpoints.messages.versions` will inline all Versions of Messages.  Non-leaf parts of the `<PATH>` MUST only reference xRegistry collection names and not any specific entity IDs since `<PATH>` is meant to be an abstract traversal of the model.

review.note: Inline traversal uses only collection plural names before its leaf; entity-ID traversal and an internal wildcard segment are directly rejected, and nested collection paths materialize the necessary hierarchy.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Inline Flag

requirements.text: There MAY be multiple `<PATH>`s specified in a single request and each protocol binding specification will indicate how the list is specified.

review.note: The HTTP server accepts comma-separated inline paths; DocumentViewUsesResponseLocalPointersWithoutDefaultVersionDuplication requests two paths and asserts the resulting document. This evidence qualifies server support only.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Inline Flag

requirements.text: The `*` value MAY be used to indicate that all nested inlineable attributes at that level in the hierarchy (and below) MUST be inlined - except `model`, `modelsource` and `capabilities` at the root of the Registry. These three are excluded since the data associated with them are configuration related. To include their data the request MUST include `<PATH>` values of `model`, `modelsource` or `capabilities` explicitly. Use of `*` MUST only be used as the last part of the `<PATH>` (in its entirety). For example, `foo*` and `*.foo` are not valid `<PATH>` values, but `*` and `endpoints.*` are.

review.note: BridgeRootInlineIsExplicitAndDoesNotAddSourceRequests verifies root wildcard expansion, excludes model/modelsource/capabilities from wildcard output, and includes them when explicitly requested. InvalidInlineAndCollectionsInputsFailBeforeAnySourceAcquisition rejects internal, prefixed and suffixed wildcard forms. This qualifies server behavior; producer-specific document traversal is not established by these cases.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Inline Flag

requirements.text: An `inline` flag without any value MAY be supported and if so it MUST have the same semantic meaning as a value of `*`.

review.note: An explicitly present inline flag with no value is equivalent to `inline=*`; the test checks nested collections and an inlined document in both responses.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Inline Flag

requirements.text: The specific value of `<PATH>` will vary based on where the request is directed. For example, a request to the root of the Registry MUST start with a `<GROUPS>` name, while a request directed at a Group would start with a `<RESOURCES>` name.

review.note: Inline paths are rooted at the current request shape: direct producer cases target Registry, Group collection, Group, Resource collection and Resource with the appropriate relative plural path, producing expected response-local pointers.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Inline Flag

requirements.text: When specifying a collection to be inlined, it MUST be specified using the plural name for the collection in its defined case.

review.note: The server accepts valid plural paths and rejects both the singular collection name and a case-variant plural name before source acquisition. Producer rejection behavior is not established by this test.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Inline Flag

requirements.text: A request to inline an unknown, or non-inlineable, attribute MUST generate an error ([bad_inline](#bad_inline)).

review.note: The HTTP contract returns bad_inline for an unknown inline path and inline_noninlineable for the known non-inlineable name `name`. The source clauses overlap by assigning both errors to non-inlineable values, so this evidence qualifies the server's distinct error handling; producer behavior is not established.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Inline Flag

requirements.text: Note: If the Registry cannot return all expected data in one response because it is too large then it MUST generate an error ([too_large](#too_large)). In those cases, the client will need to query the individual inlineable collection attributes in isolation so the Registry can leverage a pagination type of feature to iteratively retrieve the entities.

review.note: OversizedInlineDocumentResponseCanBeReadByIndividualCollection verifies too_large for the aggregate inline document response and successful retrieval of an individual Versions collection. The client paging loop and producer behavior are not qualified here.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / SetDefaultVersionID Flag

requirements.text: The `setdefaultversionid` flag MAY be used on any write operation directed to a single Resource, its `meta` sub-object or its Versions. The primary use case is one in which the current default Version is being deleted and the client wishes to choose a new default Version at the same time - to avoid an incorrect one being chosen temporarily.

review.note: The flag selects an exact Version on Resource, Meta, Version and Versions writes; the test also verifies atomic replacement of a deleted default and persistence after restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / SetDefaultVersionID Flag

requirements.text: Use of this flag on an operation that allows for modifying multiple Resources MUST generate an error ([bad_flag](#bad_flag)).

review.note: Registry, Group, Group-collection and Resource-collection writes reject the flag with bad_flag before mutation; the test checks unchanged export and event count.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / SetDefaultVersionID Flag

requirements.text: This flag MUST include a single parameter, a string containing the case-sensitive `versionid` of the Version that is to become the new default Version.

review.note: A duplicate parameter rejects with bad_flag; a single exact-case target succeeds, while a wrong-case target rejects with unknown_id.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / SetDefaultVersionID Flag

requirements.text: - A value of `null` indicates that the client wishes to switch to the ["default = newest" algorithm](#default-version-of-a-resource). In other words, the "sticky" aspect of the current default Version will be removed and `meta.defaultversionsticky` MUST be set to `false`.

review.note: The null flag overrides an older pointer and sticky true in Meta input, selects the newest Version, sets sticky false and preserves the result after restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / SetDefaultVersionID Flag

requirements.text: - If during a Version create operation the server is asked to choose the `versionid` value for the new Version, then including that value as the `setdefaultversionid` value is not possible. In those cases a value of `request` MAY be used as a way to reference that new Version.

review.note: POST to a Resource can let the server choose the Version ID while setdefaultversionid=request refers to that new Version; the direct counter test exercises this operation without a client-chosen ID.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / SetDefaultVersionID Flag

requirements.text: - A value of `request` MUST only be used on APIs that allow the creation of only a single new Version. In the case of HTTP, that is the `POST` API directed to a Resource. This is because no other operation allows for the creation of a single Version without specifying its `versionid`. Using it when more than one Version is created MUST generate an error ([too_many_versions](#too_many_versions)).  Other uses of this value on an inappropriate API MUST generate an error ([bad_flag](#bad_flag)).

review.note: Only Resource POST supports request; unsupported API uses reject with bad_flag, and request with no created Version rejects with defaultversionid_request. The exposed HTTP routes do not permit multiple Version creation with request, so the too_many_versions case has no direct evidence and this combined obligation remains pending.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / SetDefaultVersionID Flag

requirements.text: - If a value of `request` was used but no Version was created for the request, then an error ([defaultversionid_request](#defaultversionid_request)) MUST be generated.

review.note: A Resource POST using request when the body supplies a Version ID and creates no new Version rejects with defaultversionid_request; state and event count remain unchanged.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / SetDefaultVersionID Flag

requirements.text: - If a non-`null` and non-`request` value does not reference an existing Version of the Resource, after all Version processing is completed, then an error ([unknown_id](#unknown_id)) MUST be generated.

review.note: A missing or wrong-case target rejects with unknown_id after attempted updates; the export and event count remain unchanged.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / SetDefaultVersionID Flag

requirements.text: - Setting the `meta.defaultversionid` to a non-empty value via this flag MUST also set the `meta.defaultversionsticky` attribute to `true`.

review.note: An explicit non-null target sets defaultversionsticky to true even when Meta input supplies false; the test covers Meta, Resource, Version and Versions writes.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / SetDefaultVersionID Flag

requirements.text: - Use on a request that updates more than one Resource MUST generate an error ([bad_flag](#bad_flag)).

review.note: Registry-, Group- and collection-level writes that can modify multiple Resources reject the flag with bad_flag before mutation.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / SetDefaultVersionID Flag

requirements.text: - Use of this flag MUST override any `meta.defaultversionid` and `meta.defaultversionsticky` values that are present in the request.

review.note: The flag overrides supplied Meta defaultversionid and defaultversionsticky values for explicit and null selections.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / SetDefaultVersionID Flag

requirements.text: Any other invalid usage of this flag MUST generate an error ([bad_defaultversionid](#bad_defaultversionid)).

review.note: Missing, empty and malformed values reject with bad_defaultversionid; duplicate parameters reject with bad_flag under the single-parameter rule.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Sort Flag

requirements.text: When a request is directed to a collection of Groups, Resources or Versions, the `Sort` flag MAY be used to indicate the order in which the entities of that collection are to be returned (i.e. sorted). Use of the `sort` flag on a non-collection result MUST generate an error ([sort_noncollection](#sort_noncollection)).

review.note: Sorting is restricted to collection results; a direct entity sort fails sort_noncollection even when its filter would produce no matching entity. Collection output follows the requested scalar order.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Sort Flag

requirements.text: This flag MUST include a single parameter, a string containing the attribute (`<ATTRIBUTE>`) name to use as the "sort key" plus an OPTIONAL indication of whether the results are to be sorted in ascending or descending order.

review.note: Sort accepts one model-known scalar projection and rejects unknown, complex, wildcard and nested Registry collection projections. QueryPath can express nested noncollection properties without sorting a whole descendant collection.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Sort Flag

requirements.text: - `<ATTRIBUTE>` MUST be a [dot (`.`) notation](#xregistry-dot--notation) path to one of the attributes defined in collection's entities that will be the primary sort key for the results. The attribute MUST only reference a scalar attribute within the top-level collection, it MUST NOT attempt to traverse into a nested xRegistry collection even if that nested collection is inlined.

review.note: Sort accepts one model-known scalar projection and rejects unknown, complex, wildcard and nested Registry collection projections. QueryPath can express nested noncollection properties without sorting a whole descendant collection.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Sort Flag

requirements.text: - An OPTIONAL "sort order" (`asc` for ascending, `desc` for descending) MAY be specified to indicate whether the first entity in the returned collection MUST be the "lowest" values (`asc`) or whether it MUST be the "highest" value (`desc`). When not specified, the default value MUST be `asc`.

review.note: Default ascending and explicit descending sorting use missing-low semantics and an ID secondary key in the same direction. Exact expected ID sequences cover tied case-folded names, boolean values and missing numeric fields.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Sort Flag

requirements.text: When a pagination type of feature is used to return the results, but the `sort` flag is not specified, then the server MUST sort the results on the entities' `<SINGULAR>id` value in ascending order. When pagination is not used, it is RECOMMENDED that servers still sort the results by `<SINGULAR>id` (asc) for consistency.

review.note: With no sort flag, paginated collection queries set DefaultSortById; a deliberately unsorted source is returned by ID, and the HTTP test verifies that ordering across page boundaries.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Sort Flag

requirements.text: Sorting MUST be done using the data type comparison rules as specified in the [filter Flag](#filter-flag) section. However, there are certain situations that might introduce ambiguity between implementations. For example, not all persistent stores support `NaNs` (Not-a-Number values), or if the data type of an attribute changes on a per-instance basis, then consistent sorting across implementations on that attribute might be challenging. While interoperability is critical, requiring consistency in these edge cases could be excessively burdensome for implementations. To that end, this specification does not mandate the exact ordering in these situations, aside from the requirement that an implementation MUST sort the result the same way each time.

review.note: Numeric, Boolean, string and timestamp sorts use their comparison rules. Conditional timestamp/string values produce the same ID order across repeated queries with different source orders; JSON cannot represent NaN.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Sort Flag

requirements.text: Entities that do not have a value for the specified attribute MUST be treated the same as if they had the "lowest" possible value for that attribute. If more than one entity shares the same attribute value then the `<SINGULAR>id` MUST be used as a secondary sorting key, using the same `asc`/`desc` value specified for the primary sorting key.

review.note: Default ascending and explicit descending sorting use missing-low semantics and an ID secondary key in the same direction. Exact expected ID sequences cover tied case-folded names, boolean values and missing numeric fields.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / Sort Flag

requirements.text: An invalid usage of, or value for, the `sort` flag MUST generate an error ([bad_sort](#bad_sort)).

review.note: Unknown, complex, wildcard and cross-collection sort keys and invalid directions are directly rejected as bad_sort rather than silently falling back to an arbitrary order.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / SpecVersion Flag

requirements.text: The SpecVersion flag MAY be used to indicate the xRegistry specification version that the response MUST adhere to. The parameter value of this flag MUST be a case-insensitive string.

review.note: The flag accepts case variations of 1.0-rc4 and ignores numeric patch components; other major/minor values and suffixes reject with unsupported_specversion.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / SpecVersion Flag

requirements.text: If the specified version is not supported, then an error ([unsupported_specversion](#unsupported_specversion)) MUST be generated. When not specified, the default value MUST be the newest version of this specification supported by the server.

review.note: Unsupported major/minor or suffix values reject; when omitted, the response matches the server's only supported and newest version, 1.0-rc4.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / SpecVersion Flag

requirements.text: When comparing `specversion` strings, the server MUST silently ignore the "patch" version number and only consider the "major.minor" version numbers. This is because any "patch" version updates will only contain clarifications and ought not require any code changes for server implementations. Therefore, all patch versions of the same "major.minor" version MUST be forwards and backwards compatible.

review.note: Requests using different numeric patch components of 1.0-rc4 produce the same response, verifying that the patch component is ignored by version comparison.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Request Flags / SpecVersion Flag

requirements.text: However, due to the potential for semantics changes of versions with suffix values (e.g. `v2.0.0-rc1`), the suffix value MUST be part of the comparison checking.

review.note: The rc4 suffix is accepted case-insensitively; rc3 and rc5 are rejected as unsupported_specversion, so suffix changes affect the comparison.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / xRegistry Dot (`.`) Notation

requirements.text: For clarity, use of square brackets (`[]`) without use of either type of quotes around the value MUST be interpreted as accessing an array. Conversely, use of quotes MUST be interpreted as accessing an object/map.

review.note: QueryPath distinguishes quoted object/map keys from unquoted zero-based array selectors, including literal quoted '*' versus wildcard selection. Direct normative-dot vectors assert correct entity selection for both quote styles and wildcard/index paths.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / xRegistry Dot (`.`) Notation

requirements.text: Depending on the situation in which the notation is being used, there are certain special values that MAY be used, as described in the following sections.

review.note: Context-dependent additional selectors and third-party editing syntax guidance are not a mandate to implement an extended JSONPath editor or mutation CLI. Rejection of non-Core query editing operators is not a mandatory conformance defect.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / xRegistry Discovery / Registry-base Discovery

requirements.text: Similar to the [Host-based Discovery](#host-based-discovery) mechanism, an xRegistry server instance MAY advertise a list of additional xRegistry servers by supporting a protocol-specific retrieval mechanism.

review.note: The engine's configured Registry-based discovery advertises its own absolute public root by default, which the source explicitly permits. Client discovery uses the mounted .xregistry endpoint and does not treat advertisements as permission to acquire them.

Automatic combined discovery is a SHOULD-level orchestration gap, not permission to broaden credential/egress scope.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing

requirements.text: If an error occurs during the processing of a request, even if the error was during the creation of the response (e.g. an invalid `inline` value was provided), then an error MUST be generated and the entire request MUST be undone.

review.note: Source inspection confirms one staged candidate and response preparation before publication; direct assertions cover nested failure, response/header failure, cancellation, stale candidates and durable restart rollback. The all-failures statement is not promoted across arbitrary injected persistence or an explicitly indeterminate commit acknowledgement.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing

requirements.text: In general, when an error is generated, it SHOULD be sent back to the client. However, this MAY not happen if the server determines there is a good reason to not do so - such as due to security concerns.

review.note: Errors are returned through the current HTTP contract while untrusted policy exception URLs/credentials are removed. Direct assertions require safe title/subject/type and absence of secret-bearing detail, not indiscriminate disclosure.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing

requirements.text: Each protocol binding specification will define how the error structure SHOULD be returned back to clients.

review.note: The binding specification defines wire placement of the abstract error structure. This source-author cross-reference does not independently promote the already reviewed HTTP family.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing

requirements.text: | Type  | REQUIRED. MUST be a URI to the error definition/specification. |

review.note: Current wire vectors assert exact catalog URI, nonempty meaningful title, HTTP status and subject for route/body/flag errors; missing contract arguments produce an explicit infrastructure problem rather than a malformed standard error.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing

requirements.text: | Code  | REQUIRED. MUST be the HTTP response code and status text. |

review.note: Abstract 'Code' here means HTTP response code plus status text, whereas the HTTP JSON binding uses status and a symbolic code and transports status separately. Existing assertions establish numeric HTTP/status and symbolic code, not an abstract status-text field; record the binding mapping rather than treating the lowercase JSON code as an unconditional defect.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing

requirements.text: | Title | REQUIRED. MUST be a short (non-empty) human-readable summary of the error. This SHOULD be sufficiently detailed for most users to determine what is the cause of the error. See the text below about substitution strings. |

review.note: Current wire vectors assert exact catalog URI, nonempty meaningful title, HTTP status and subject for route/body/flag errors; missing contract arguments produce an explicit infrastructure problem rather than a malformed standard error.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing

requirements.text: | Detail | OPTIONAL. While "Title" conveys the critical error information, if additional details might be useful to users, such as hints as to how to fix the error, then this field SHOULD be used. |

review.note: Optional diagnostic-field definition, not a requirement to expose implementation/source/request details. Omitted detail/args/instance/source is allowed as applicable; no disclosure or implementation credit is inferred from omission.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing

requirements.text: | Subject | OPTIONAL. If present, MUST be a reference to the entity being processed when the error occurred. In the case of a Registry entity, it MUST be the XID of the entity. If no specific value is appropriate then this field MAY be excluded. MUST start with "/" when referencing an xRegistry entity or collection. |

review.note: Exact entity/Meta/Resource subjects are directly asserted, and catalog-specific malformed-ID errors intentionally use the requested absolute URL. The generic XID sentence and per-error Subject definitions must be read together; every error's optional/nonempty/collection subject is not covered by the current vector subset.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing

requirements.text: | Args | OPTIONAL. A map of the substitution strings that were used when generating the "Title" text. |

review.note: Optional diagnostic-field definition, not a requirement to expose implementation/source/request details. Omitted detail/args/instance/source is allowed as applicable; no disclosure or implementation credit is inferred from omission.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing

requirements.text: | Instance | OPTIONAL. This is a non-empty string that can be used by servers to identify details related to the request/error processing. For example, a request or transaction ID of the request that generated the error. This information is not meant to be useful to clients directly, but can be provided to server administrators to help debugging if necessary. This specification places no restriction on the format of this value. |

review.note: Optional diagnostic-field definition, not a requirement to expose implementation/source/request details. Omitted detail/args/instance/source is allowed as applicable; no disclosure or implementation credit is inferred from omission.

review.note: Optional diagnostic-field definition, not a requirement to expose implementation/source/request details. Omitted detail/args/instance/source is allowed as applicable; no disclosure or implementation credit is inferred from omission.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing

requirements.text: The definition of each error's "Title" field MAY include substitutable placeholders that allows for situational specific data to be included. Each placeholder will be denoted as `<...>` in the "Title" text, where "..." MUST be of the form `[a-z][a-z0-9_]*`, no longer than 63 characters, and used as the key in the "Args" map. At runtime, each placeholder MUST be replaced with the appropriate value from "Args", and "Args" (if non-empty) MUST appear in the error structure returned to the client. As an optimization, if "<subject>" is used then it MUST NOT be included "Args" as it MUST already appear as a stand-alone field in the error structure.

review.note: Current vectors assert substituted titles, exact non-subject args and safe failure when required arguments are missing. The complete placeholder grammar/length and every runtime catalog/extension error is not proven by these vectors; no whole-catalog promotion.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing

requirements.text: The "Type", "Code", and "Subject" values MUST be as specified in error's specification. The "Title" field MAY be modified as needed based on the context in which the implementation is running. This includes being specified in a language other than English, however it MUST still include the same substitution values (possibly in a different order).

review.note: The directly reviewed catalog vectors assert exact Type/status/Subject and substitution values. The unrestricted all-errors and localized-title contract remains pending, and binding-specific Code mapping is recorded separately rather than reopened as an old HTTP error defect.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing

requirements.text: Most of the error conditions mentioned in this specification will include a reference to one of the errors listed in this section. While it is RECOMMENDED that implementations use those errors (for consistency), they MAY choose to use a more appropriate one. Implementations MAY define additional extension fields, as well as new error definitions. For new errors, it is RECOMMENDED that the "Subject" value appears within the "Title" field, when appropriate.

review.note: The source permits appropriate alternative/extension errors and recommends style for custom diagnostics; server_error is optional for unexpected failures. These permissions are not coverage promotions and do not permit leaking untrusted exception data.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing / action_not_supported

requirements.text: In the case of using the HTTP protocol binding, this error MUST include the HTTP `Allow` header in the response indicating which HTTP methods the API supports, if any.

review.note: Actual action_not_supported HTTP vectors assert 405 and the complete expected Allow method list for supported route shapes, not merely presence of an Allow header.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing / bad_request

requirements.text: This error is purposely generic and can be used when there isn't a more condition-specific error that would be more appropriate. Implementations SHOULD attempt to use a more specific error when possible. Notice, the `Title` field is just a substitution value and MUST NOT be empty.

review.note: Current bad_request paths contain concrete nonempty details, and more specific catalog errors are preferred. No direct reviewed generic bad_request response vector proves its title substitution/emptiness contract; other error titles are not the same case.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing / not_found

requirements.text: Note, this SHOULD only be used when the request was directed to an entity that does not exist. For cases where the target entity does exist, but there is an invalid attempt to reference one that doesn't, the [unknown_id](#unknown_id) error SHOULD be used instead.

review.note: Direct absent entities return not_found, while a valid Resource with a nonexistent requested default Version returns unknown_id with the correct Resource subject and Version arguments.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing / parsing_data

requirements.text: This is a fairly generic error, so if a more focused one (e.g. [invalid_attribute](#invalid_attribute)) can be used instead, then it SHOULD be. `<data_description>` is meant to be a phrase, or identifier, of the data being parsed; e.g. `/model`.

review.note: Malformed/duplicate JSON uses parsing_data with the exact entity subject and nonempty detail; typed metadata violations use more specific errors. The actual wire vectors make the intended distinction explicit.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing / server_error

requirements.text: This error MAY be used when it appears that the incoming request was valid but something unexpected happened in the server that caused an error condition.

review.note: The source permits appropriate alternative/extension errors and recommends style for custom diagnostics; server_error is optional for unexpected failures. These permissions are not coverage promotions and do not permit leaking untrusted exception data.

review.note: Unknown Group and Resource types are directly rejected with their distinct catalog errors, exact typed request subjects and required type-name arguments. This does not infer producer model absence semantics from the full server.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Notations and Terminology / Notational Conventions

requirements.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2119).

review.note: RFC 2119 interpretation, not an executable feature. This proposal reviews the entire active HTTP source, including subordinate rules, wire sketches and examples; implementation suggestions are not execution receipts.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Notations and Terminology / Notational Conventions

requirements.text: For clarity, OPTIONAL attributes (specification-defined and extensions) are OPTIONAL for clients to use, but the servers' responsibility will vary. Server-unknown extension attributes MUST be silently stored in the backing datastore. Specification-defined attributes and server-known extension attributes MUST generate an error if the corresponding feature is not supported or enabled. However, as with all attributes, if accepting the attribute results in a bad state (such as exceeding a size limit or resulting in a security issue), then the server MAY choose to reject the request.

review.note: Model-permitted extension values pass through validation, Merge and publication without feature-specific handlers. Closed-model unknown names remain errors, not silently accepted extensions. Disabled metadata and finite host budgets are explicit rejections.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Notations and Terminology / Notational Conventions

requirements.text: In the pseudo JSON format snippets `?` means the preceding item is OPTIONAL, `*` means the preceding item MAY appear zero or more times, and `+` means the preceding item MUST appear at least once. The presence of the `#` character means the remaining portion of the line is a comment. Whitespace characters in the JSON snippets are used for readability and are not normative.

review.note: Defines pseudocode cardinality and comments. The sketches were interpreted as notation, not JSON payloads containing comments, ellipses or optionality markers.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / HTTP API Patterns

requirements.text: While these APIs are shown to be at the root path of a host, implementations MAY choose to prefix them as necessary. However, the same prefix MUST be used consistently for all APIs in the same Registry instance.

review.note: MapXRegistry applies one MountPath/PathBase prefix; navigation is generated from configured PublicRoot, never Host. The client appends escaped relative paths below its one configured root. Error subjects have a separate prefix defect recorded on the request_path clause.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / HTTP API Patterns

requirements.text: If an OPTIONAL HTTP path is not supported by an implementation, then any use of that API MUST generate an error ([api_not_found](#api_not_found)).

review.note: The implementation supplies the listed optional administrative paths. Unsupported administrative subpaths produce HTTP 404 api_not_found. A supported but capability-disabled metadata API instead uses Core not_available; that distinction is deliberate and directly asserted.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / HTTP API Patterns

requirements.text: If an HTTP method is not supported for a supported HTTP path, then an error ([action_not_supported](./spec.md#action_not_supported)) MUST be generated.

review.note: TryAction, model-aware Allowed and the adapter reject unsupported verbs before body consumption. The catalog emits 405 action_not_supported and Allow; document PATCH uses the more specific details_required error.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / HTTP API Patterns

requirements.text: Implementations MAY support extension APIs, however, the following rules apply:

review.note: Permission to add APIs, not a requirement to provide an arbitrary extension-API facility. The mapped handler implements explicit registry routes and the defined shortself mechanism; extension path restrictions are reviewed in the following records.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / HTTP API Patterns

requirements.text: - New HTTP paths that extend non-root paths MUST NOT be defined as they might conflict with URLs of entities within the system.

review.note: No custom subordinate administrative API is registered. The adapter rejects /model/extra and similar paths, while RegistryPath permits only the defined entity, meta and versions shapes. Shortself navigation reuses canonical routes rather than adding arbitrary child APIs.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / HTTP API Patterns

requirements.text: - New root HTTP paths MAY be defined as long as they do not use Registry-level HTTP paths or attribute names. This includes extension and Groups collection attribute names.

review.note: Optional root-extension permission. No arbitrary root extension registry is adopted by MapXRegistry; independently mapped application APIs remain a host integration responsibility. This is not evidence that arbitrary host extensions have been collision-checked.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / Adherence to HTTP Standards

requirements.text: - A `PUT` or `POST` operation is a full replacement of the entities processed. Any missing attributes MUST be interpreted as a request for them to be deleted. However, attributes that are managed by the server might have specialized processing in those cases, in particular, mandatory attributes, as well as ones that have default values defined, MUST be reset to their default values rather than deleted.

review.note: Merge starts replacement metadata from an empty object, retains managed fields and then completes defaults. Document headers intentionally use PATCH-like metadata semantics. The complete PUT/POST omission-and-default matrix is not directly established by the existing HTTP assertions.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / Adherence to HTTP Standards

requirements.text: - A `PATCH` operation MUST only modify the attributes explicitly mentioned in the request. Any attribute in the request with a value of `null` MUST be interpreted as a request to delete the attribute, and as with `PUT`/`POST`, server-managed attributes might have specialized processing.

review.note: PATCH clones existing attributes, overwrites supplied complete values and lets completion remove nullable optional attributes. Missing values persist; server-managed epochs/timestamps and related lifecycle changes are not mistaken for forbidden side effects.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / Adherence to HTTP Standards

requirements.text: - `PUT` MUST NOT be targeted at xRegistry collections. A `POST` or `PATCH` MUST be used instead to add entities to the collection, and a `DELETE` MUST then be used to delete unwanted entities.

review.note: Allowed groups all three collection kinds into PATCH/POST/DELETE with no Replace action. The raw route matrix asserts PUT /teams is 405; collection mutation/deletion semantics are exercised through the public engine and actual Resource collection routes.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / Adherence to HTTP Standards

requirements.text: - Unknown query parameters SHOULD be silently ignored by servers. This includes specification-defined but unsupported query parameters.

review.note: HTTP-SEM-001 is fixed: only an enabled, recognized inline parameter marks an explicit override. Disabled inline is ignored on ordinary GET and cannot suppress mandatory export defaults. Actual MapXRegistry regression was red before the fix and the focused matrix passes on net8.0/net10.0.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / No-Code Servers

requirements.text: In the [core specification](./spec.md) there is a discussion about ["no-code servers"](./spec.md#design-no-code-servers). In the case of HTTP, simple file servers SHOULD support exposing Resources where the HTTP body response contains the Resource's domain-specific "document" as well as exposing the serialization of the Resource's xRegistry metadata via the [`$details`](#resource-metadata-vs-resource-document) suffix on the URL path. This can be achieved by creating a secondary, sibling, file on disk with `$details` at the end of its filename.

review.note: Conditional advice to no-code file-server producers. This HTTP review does not claim a static-file deployment or re-review the File specification. The actual dynamic host's Document/$details pairing is covered by the Resource representation records.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs

requirements.text: This section mainly focuses on the successful interaction patterns of the APIs. For example, most examples will show an HTTP "200 OK" as the response. Each implementation MAY choose to return a more appropriate response based on the specific situation. For example, in the case of an authentication error the server could return `401 Unauthorized`.

review.note: Success sketches do not override authentication, authorization, limits or uncertain commit outcomes. The host uses explicit 401/403/413/503 results; the client preserves error statuses without retries or success-shaped body substitution.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: Creating or updating entities MAY be done using HTTP `PUT`, `PATCH` or `POST` methods:

review.note: Introduces the five entity/collection mutation patterns. Their concrete body, dispatch and response obligations are reviewed separately below, rather than treating this introductory permission as additional executed evidence.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: See the [`Request Flags`](#request-flags--query-parameters) section for the list of flags/query parameters that MAY be used for each API.

review.note: Cross-reference to per-operation flag rules. RequestFlags and query/projection consumers were inspected; concrete flag syntax, applicability and defects are recorded under the flag clauses.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: The `PUT` variant MUST adhere to the following:

review.note: PUT umbrella introducing lines 222-235. The individual rules have their own decisions and gaps; this heading is not a separate claim that every PUT permutation has direct tests.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The URL MUST be of the form: `<PATH-TO-ENTITY>`.

review.note: RegistryPath separates entity and collection shapes; Allowed does not grant PUT to collections. Client relative-path construction preserves the requested entity below the registry prefix.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The HTTP body MUST contain the full updated serialization of the entity to be processed.

review.note: The adapter distinguishes a nonempty JSON metadata body from exact Document input, then Replace dispatches a full entity replacement. Body presence is directly tested, but complete metadata replacement of previously populated mutable attributes needs a direct operation vector.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The entity processed MUST either be created (if it does not already exist), or updated (if it does exist).

review.note: EnsureGroup/EnsureResource and ApplyVersion select existing staged/snapshot identities or create new entities. Actual HTTP PUT creates a Resource, then updates the same identity and advances its epoch without creating another Version.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - Any mutable attribute which is either missing or present with a value of `null`, MUST be interpreted as a request to delete the attribute.

review.note: Metadata Replace builds a fresh mutable attribute map, and completion removes optional nulls. Existing null-deletion assertions concern PATCH/header semantics; they do not establish omitted-attribute deletion for metadata PUT.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - Excluding any Registry collection attributes, all mutable attributes specified MUST be a full serialization of the attribute. Any missing nested attribute MUST be interpreted as a request to delete the attribute.

review.note: Merge assigns each submitted complex value as one DeepClone, not a recursive merge. Scalar-map headers have direct replacement tests; nested metadata objects/arrays on entity PUT are a separate direct-evidence gap.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - After processing the request, if there are any missing REQUIRED attributes then an error ([required_attribute_missing](./spec.md#required_attribute_missing)) MUST be generated.

review.note: Complete checks required model attributes before publication and supplies required_attribute_missing with the affected entity and list argument. An actual HTTP Resource creation missing a required Version field asserts the exact error contract.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: The `PATCH` variant when directed at a single entity, MUST adhere to the `PUT` semantics defined above with the following exceptions:

review.note: PATCH umbrella. The following records review preserved omissions, null deletion, details_required and create-with-required-values independently.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - Any mutable attribute which is missing MUST be interpreted as a request to leave it unchanged. However, modifying some other attribute (or some other server semantics) MAY modify it. A value of `null` MUST be interpreted as a request to delete the attribute.

review.note: PATCH preserves omitted ordinary attributes and interprets explicit null as deletion. Required/default and generated-field semantics are applied during completion, not by inventing values in the client codec.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - When processing a Resource or Version, whose Resource type has its [`hasdocument`](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringhasdocument) model aspect set to `true`, the URL accessing the entity MUST include the `$details` suffix, and MUST generate an error ([details_required](#details_required)) in the absence of the `$details` suffix. This is because when it is absent, the processing of the HTTP `xRegistry-` headers are already defined with "PATCH" semantics so a normal `PUT` or `POST` can be used instead. Using `PATCH` in this case would mean that the request is trying to "patch" the Resource's "document", which this specification does not support at this time.

review.note: Allowed removes PATCH for document-bearing Resource/Version paths lacking $details, and the adapter returns the specific 405 details_required rather than attempting to patch bytes. Metadata-only types remain patchable without the suffix.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - `PATCH` MAY be used to create new entities, but as with any of the create operations, any missing REQUIRED attributes MUST generate an error ([required_attribute_missing](./spec.md#required_attribute_missing)).

review.note: PATCH shares Ensure/New and Complete with PUT, so creation is implemented and required fields are enforced. Existing required-field HTTP evidence is PUT, not PATCH creation.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: The `POST` variant when directed at a single entity other than a Resource, MUST adhere to the following:

review.note: Introduces POST-to-owner collection-map rules; supported owners are Registry and Group. Concrete map validation, unchanged owner metadata and response selection follow below.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The HTTP body MUST contain only a JSON map where the key MUST be the attribute (collection) name of a nested xRegistry collection. The value of each map entry MUST be a map of nested entities where the key is the entity's `<SINGULAR>id` and the value is a serialization of the entity itself.

review.note: ApplyContainerAsync(collectionsOnly=true) accepts model collection names, and ApplyCollectionAsync requires ID-keyed object entries. Public engine tests assert the owner/collection envelope and reject ordinary owner attributes with groups_only/resources_only.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The processing of each top-level map entry MUST follow the same rules as defined for `POST` to the nested xRegistry collection where the map entry's value is the input.

review.note: Each owner-map entry calls the same ApplyCollectionAsync implementation used by POST to that collection. Existing owner POST assertions do not compare mixed collection types against equivalent direct collection POST operations.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The root of the JSON object in the HTTP body MUST NOT contain any attributes of the targeted entity other than the nested collections, and none of that entity's attribute are to be updated. This operation allows for an update to multiple nested collections in a single operation without modifying the owning entity.

review.note: collectionsOnly skips Merge on the owner and rejects noncollection attributes after requested ignore processing. Membership-driven counts/epochs remain Core-managed effects. Rejection is tested; preservation of a preexisting owner's ordinary attributes needs its own direct assertion.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The response message MUST be a map of the nested entity types with just the changed entities that were processed. No top-level entity attributes are to appear - similar to the request message.

review.note: HTTP-SEM-002 is fixed: validated owner POST retains its normalized collection input for response selection, rather than re-reading raw configuration fields. Actual HTTP tests verify multiple Group collections, exact processed keys, unchanged ignored configuration and deterministic empty responses for only-ignored input.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: The `POST` variant when directed at a Resource entity, MUST adhere to the following:

review.note: Resource POST umbrella, distinct from POST to Registry/Group owners. The concrete single-Version body and PUT-like processing rules are reviewed next.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The HTTP body MUST contain the serialization of the single Version to be created, however, it MAY include Resource-level read-only attributes (such as `versionscount`), and if they are present, then they MUST be silently ignored by the server. This is done as a convenience for users who might have obtained the Version's serialization from a query to a Resource (not a specific Version), in which case those extra Resource-level attributes would be included in the serialization.

review.note: Resource POST calls VersionInput and ApplyVersion for one Version; VersionInput strips read-only Resource projection fields. Existing POST tests use Version input, not a copied Resource response carrying versionscount/metaurl.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The 'PUT' variant rules above MUST apply to the new Version entity.

review.note: Metadata Resource POST passes patch=false for the selected Version; Document mode preserves the special header PATCH semantics. Direct POST replacement of an existing explicitly selected Version is not asserted by the creation-focused tests.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: The `PATCH` variant when directed at an xRegistry collection, MUST adhere to the following:

review.note: Introduces collection PATCH. Individual keyed-map, subset-value and per-entity PATCH obligations are separately reviewed below.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The HTTP body MUST contain a JSON map where the key MUST be the `<SINGULAR>id` of each entity in the map. Note, that in the case of a map of Versions, the `versionid` is used.

review.note: Collection PATCH parses a JSON object, derives each child path from its key and retains nested ID checks. Actual Resource collection PATCH asserts only the requested unlocked entry is returned; a wrong nested ID remains an error under ignore.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - Each value in the map MUST contain just the attributes that are to be updated for that entity.

review.note: Collection PATCH forwards partial entity objects with patch=true; it does not require a full entity serialization. Existing public operation and actual HTTP tests exercise partial name/rank changes without supplying generated attributes.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The processing of each individual entity in the map MUST follow the same rules as defined for `PATCH` of a single entity above.

review.note: All three collection branches forward the PATCH selector to the same entity mutation routines. Direct subset/filter assertions cover Groups and Resources; Version collection omission/null/default behavior lacks an equivalent direct operation case.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: The `POST` variant when directed at an xRegistry collection MUST adhere to the following:

review.note: Collection POST umbrella; the following keyed-map, replacement and missing-Version requirements carry the behavioral decisions.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The HTTP body MUST contain a JSON map where the key MUST be the `<SINGULAR>id` of each entity in the map. Note, that in the case of a map of Versions, the `versionid` is used.

review.note: Collection POST uses the same ID-keyed parser as collection PATCH. A real Resource collection POST creates locked/open entries and public engine Group POST creates separate a/b entries; Version keys are passed directly to ApplyVersion.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - Each value in the map MUST be the full serialization of the entity to be either added or updated. Note that `POST` does not support deleting entities from a collection, so a separate delete operation might be needed if there are entities that need to be removed.

review.note: ApplyCollectionAsync iterates supplied entries only and passes replacement semantics for POST; it never deletes omitted members. Membership retention is asserted, but replacing an existing member's omitted ordinary fields is not directly covered.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The processing of each individual entity in the map MUST follow the same rules as defined for `PUT` above.

review.note: Collection POST invokes the same ApplyContainer/ApplyResource/ApplyVersion paths as PUT with patch=false. This is implementation evidence, not a substitute for the missing existing-member replacement comparison.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - In the case of an empty map of Versions and the Resource being referenced does not exist yet, an error ([missing_versions](#missing_versions)) MUST be generated because a Resource can not exist without any Versions. If the intent was to create a Resource with a Version that has just default values, then there are other APIs that can be used that make that intent clear (e.g. `PUT` to the Resource itself).

review.note: ApplyCollectionAsync explicitly throws missing_versions for an empty Version map when the owning Resource is absent. The matching 400 HTTP catalog entry exists. No direct existing test assertion for this exact absent-versus-existing boundary was found.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - If an entity with the specified `<SINGULAR>id` already exists then it MUST be interpreted as a request to update the existing entity. Otherwise, it MUST be interpreted as a request to create a new entity with that `<SINGULAR>id`.

review.note: Find/Ensure/New determines update versus creation from the canonical target identity. Escaped spellings share identity, while case-conflicting sibling IDs are rejected rather than creating ambiguous duplicates.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - Unless otherwise noted, all non-xRegistry collection attributes present MUST be a full representation of their values. This means any complex attributes (e.g. objects, maps), MUST be fully replaced by the incoming value.

review.note: Merge overwrites submitted attributes as complete values, including on PATCH. Header-map replacement is directly established, but a nested metadata object replacement is not proved by a scalar-map header test.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - A request to update, or delete, a read-only attribute MUST be silently ignored. However, a request that includes a `<SINGULAR>id` MUST be compared with the entity's current value and if it differs then an error ([mismatched_id](./spec.md#mismatched_id)) MUST be generated. This includes both `<RESOURCE>id` and `versionid` in the case of Resources and Versions. This is to prevent accidentally updating the wrong entity.

review.note: Ordinary read-only input is discarded before value validation, but engine Guard/CheckId preserves Resource ID and versionid comparisons. The header codec similarly retains identity/epoch guards, including exact large integers, instead of treating them as ignorable read-only fields.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - A request to update a mutable attribute with an invalid value MUST generate an error ([invalid_attribute](./spec.md#invalid_attribute)) (this includes deleting a mandatory mutable attribute that has no default value defined).

review.note: HTTP-SEM-003 is fixed and directly verified: explicit null removal of an existing required value reports invalid_attribute with the actual attribute name. Top-level/nested objects, array/map items, Version/projection and Document-header mutations preserve rollback. Initial absence or PUT omission keeps required_attribute_missing; defaults still reset. This is diagnostic classification, not permission to accept invalid state.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - Registry collection attributes MUST be processed per the rules specified in the [Updating Nested Registry Collections](./spec.md#updating-nested-registry-collections) section.

review.note: Nested registry collections are dispatched separately from ordinary attributes; supplied children are processed without replacing whole collections. Nested Version input takes precedence over the Resource default projection, and nested failures roll back the request.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - Write operations that are meant to include xRegistry metadata in the HTTP body MUST NOT be empty, and if detected MUST generate an error ([missing_body](#missing_body)). To denote an empty set of metadata, `{}` MUST be used instead.

review.note: The adapter reads bounded metadata bytes and rejects a zero-length write with missing_body; {} is a present JSON object. This rule is not applied to Document-mode writes, where an empty body is real content.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - Any error during the processing of an entity, or its nested entities, MUST result in the entire request being rejected and no updates performed.

review.note: The engine stages the entire mutation, authorizes affected descendants, validates content, renders and prepares headers before one persistence candidate is committed. Failures before publication have no effects. Transport failure after commit is explicitly not advertised as rollback or retried.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - When a write operation request includes the Resource/Version's metadata in the HTTP body, then the inclusion of any xRegistry `xRegistry-` HTTP headers MUST generate an error ([extra_xregistry_header](#extra_xregistry_header)).

review.note: All metadata-body writes reject any xRegistry-prefixed request header before parsing the body. The actual HTTP extra-header assertion targets a Group; the required Resource/Version $details combinations are not directly asserted through the server.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - When a write operation request includes a domain-specific document in the HTTP body, and the `<RESOURCE>url` xRegistry HTTP header is present with a non-null value, the HTTP body MUST be empty. If the `<RESOURCE>url` attribute is absent, then the contents of the HTTP body (even if empty) are to be used as the entity's document.

review.note: ApplyDocument requires an explicit external-reference policy and probes for an empty body when a non-null URL is supplied; otherwise it consumes even zero bytes as the Document. The client rejects a nonempty or unknowably empty URL upload before credentials. The server's URL-plus-nonempty-body boundary lacks direct HTTP evidence.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The `<RESOURCE>` and `<RESOURCEbase64>` attributes MUST never appear as xRegistry HTTP headers, and if present on a write request MUST generate an error ([extra_xregistry_header](#extra_xregistry_header)).

review.note: The shared codec rejects both Document-content header names before type lookup, even for null, and omits them from response headers. The adapter preserves the standardized extra_xregistry_header diagnostic.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: A successful response MUST return the same response as a `GET` to the entity (or entities) processed, showing their current representation in the same format (`$details` variant or not) as the request, with the following exceptions:

review.note: HTTP-SEM-002's ignored owner-input rendering defect is fixed and covered by actual root POST tests. Writes and reads still share RenderAsync. This broad clause remains pending because full metadata and optional-header equivalence across every write route was not established by the focused fixes.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - In the `POST` case, or a `PATCH` directed to an xRegistry collection, the result MUST contain only the entities processed, not the entire Registry collection.

review.note: Collection POST/PATCH selection and readonly omission remain unchanged. Root POST now selects from normalized owner collections, and actual multi-Group-type tests exclude old entries and ignored configuration while returning exactly the processed IDs.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - In the `PUT` or `PATCH` cases that are directed to a single entity, for a newly created entity, the HTTP status MUST be `201 Created`, and it MUST include an HTTP `Location` header with a URL to the newly created entity. Note that this URL MUST be the same as the `self` attribute of that entity.

review.note: SetOutcome assigns Created and Location using the selected representation's self URL. A real Document PUT asserts 201 and its literal Location; metadata/Version/Group PATCH creation and Location=self equality are not directly covered. External-document 303 follows the later explicit redirect variants.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - In the `PUT` or `PATCH` cases directed at a single Resource or Version, if a new Version was created, the response MUST include a `Content-Location` HTTP header to the newly created Version entity, and it MUST be the same as the Version's `self` attribute.

review.note: SetOutcome supplies ContentLocation from the newly created Version and adds $details only for a document-bearing metadata response. PreparedResponse writes that URI. Existing creation tests do not assert Content-Location or equality with the new Version's self.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The responses MUST NOT include any inlineable attributes (such as `<RESOURCE>`, `<RESOURCE>base64` or nested objects/collections) unless requested.

review.note: RenderEntity/RenderResourcePart omit collection bodies, meta, configuration and inline Document attributes unless selected by Inline. Ordinary extension objects are not confused with the Core list of inlineable attributes. Export and doc have their explicit specialized projections.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: Otherwise an HTTP `200 OK` without an HTTP `Location` header MUST be returned.

review.note: Existing ordinary updates remain Success/200 and only explicit creation/redirect branches set Location. Tests assert update 200 but not the absence of Location. Later Resource POST/redirect examples provide the specialized status exceptions to this general sentence.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: Note that the response MUST be generated applying the semantics of any [request flags](#request-flags--query-parameters) specified in the request URL (e.g. `?inline`).

review.note: RequestFlags is parsed before mutation and RenderAsync applies flags to the response, not as a filter on which requested entities are mutated. A response filter can omit a changed child without preventing its persisted update; inline/binary operate on representation.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities / xRegistry Root HTTP Header

requirements.text: All API responses, including errors, SHOULD include a `Link` HTTP header of the form:

review.note: RootHeaders seeds both successful and problem responses with the trusted xregistry-root link, and pagination appends rather than replaces it. This covers responses produced by the mapped handler, not transport errors rejected by Kestrel before routing.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / HTTP-Specific Attribute Processing Rules / `self` Attribute

requirements.text: - When serializing Resources and Versions, whose Resource type's [`hasdocument`](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringhasdocument) aspect is set to `true`, then this URL MUST include the `$details` suffix appended to its `<SINGULAR>id` if it is serialized in the the HTTP body response. If the aspect is set to `false` then it MUST NOT include it. This rule applies even if the URL used in a request message did include the suffix.

review.note: RenderResourcePart uses HasDocument to add $details in metadata self; Document headers reset self to the document path. Metadata-only suffix requests emit suffix-free self. This follows the explicit rule rather than later illustrative self strings that omit $details; doc-view fragment rules remain specialized.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / HTTP-Specific Attribute Processing Rules / `labels` Attribute

requirements.text: - When `labels` is serialized as an HTTP header, see [Serializing Resource Domain-Specific Documents](#serializing-resource-domain-specific-documents), then each map entry MUST appear as a separate HTTP header using a name of `xRegistry-labels.<KEYNAME>`.

review.note: The shared codec emits a separate xRegistry-labels.<key> field per entry. It splits only the first map-name dot, preserving dots in the key; actual requests/responses assert literal label header names and escaped values.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / HTTP-Specific Attribute Processing Rules / `contenttype` Attribute

requirements.text: - When this attribute is serialized as an HTTP header, it MUST use the name `Content-Type` and not `xRegistry-contenttype`.

review.note: contenttype maps to the standard Content-Type field and xRegistry-contenttype is rejected. Its value retains standard media-type syntax, including parameters, rather than applying an invented custom-header grammar. It can also supply conditional attribute context.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / HTTP-Specific Attribute Processing Rules / `contenttype` Attribute

requirements.text: - On an update request when the xRegistry metadata appears in HTTP headers, unlike other attributes that will remain unchanged when not specified, this attribute MUST be erased if the incoming request does not include the `Content-Type` HTTP header.

review.note: Document-mode ApplyAsync explicitly assigns request ContentType, including null, rather than retaining the prior value. The codec treats absent request Content-Type as cleared conditional context, not a missing stored discriminator to synthesize or fetch.

requirements.text: Since xRegistry collections (i.e. the `<COLLECTION>` attribute) could be too large to retrieve in a single request, when retrieving a collection, the client MAY request a subset by using the [pagination specification](../pagination/spec.md). Likewise, the server MAY choose to return a subset of the collection using the same mechanism defined in that specification even if the request didn't ask for pagination. The pagination specification MUST only be used when the request is directed at a collection, not at its owning entity (such as the root of the Registry, or at an individual Group or Resource).
