source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document

requirements.text: The core specification's [Resource Metadata vs Resource Document](./spec.md#resource-metadata-vs-resource-document) section explains how Resource types might be defined to have a domain-specific document associated with them via their [`hasdocument` model aspect](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringhasdocument) being set to `true`. For HTTP, clients indicate whether they want to interact with the Resource's xRegistry metadata or the Resource's domain-specific document by the use of a `$details` suffix on the `<RESOURCE>id` in its URL. Presence of the `$details` suffix MUST be interpreted as a request to interact with the xRegistry metadata of the Resource, while its absence MUST be interpreted as a request to interact with the Resource's domain-specific document.

review.note: Literal $details selects metadata for document-bearing Resource/Version paths; otherwise the exact domain Document is read/written. RegistryPath keeps suffix syntax distinct from an encoded dollar in an ID, and both actual HTTP representations are asserted.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document

requirements.text: Use of `$details` on a non-Resource entity MUST generate an error ([bad_details](./spec.md#bad_details)).

review.note: Suffix use on Group, collection, Meta and administrative shapes is rejected as bad_details. The later explicit Version APIs clarify that Version $details is supported; the shorthand 'non-Resource' sentence is not used to prohibit those Version routes.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document

requirements.text: If a Resource type does not support domain-specific documents (i.e. [`hasdocument`](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringhasdocument) is set to `false`), then use of the `$details` suffix in a request URL MUST be treated the same as if it were absent and any URLs in server response messages referencing that Resource (e.g. `self`) MUST NOT include it.

review.note: HasDocument=false bypasses Document mode even if $details was requested. Response self and navigation remain suffix-free. Actual metadata-only and shortself tests assert this and preserve arbitrary domain URL strings without rewriting them.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document / Serializing Resource Domain-Specific Documents

requirements.text: When a Resource is serialized as its underlying domain-specific document, in other words `$details` is not appended to its URL path, the HTTP body of requests and responses MUST be the exact bytes of that document. If the document is empty, then the HTTP body MUST be empty (zero length).

review.note: Document mode never parses or reformats domain bytes. Bounded upload, persisted read, prepared response and client copying preserve binary, JSON-looking and invalid-UTF8 payloads, including present zero length. Inline metadata serialization is a separate representation.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document / Serializing Resource Domain-Specific Documents

requirements.text: In this serialization mode, it might be useful for clients to also interact with some of the Resource's xRegistry metadata. To support this, some of the Resource's xRegistry metadata MAY appear as HTTP headers in messages.

review.note: The optional Document-plus-metadata-header facility is adopted by both client and server through the same explicit model-aware codec. Header reading does not consume the Document or trigger a model fetch; actual wire assertions independently establish the encoding.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document / Serializing Resource Domain-Specific Documents

requirements.text: On responses, unless otherwise stated, all top-level scalar attributes of the Resource SHOULD appear as HTTP headers where the header name is the name of the attribute prefixed with `xRegistry-`. Note, the optionality of this requirement is not to allow for servers to decide whether or not to do so, rather it is to allow for [No-Code Servers](#no-code-servers) that might not be able to control the HTTP response headers.

review.note: Response encoding enumerates top-level scalar metadata, including read-only and active conditional fields, using xRegistry- names except the standard Content-Type mapping. The dynamic host does not invoke the no-code exception to omit supported scalar metadata.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document / Serializing Resource Domain-Specific Documents

requirements.text: The `<RESOURCE>` and `<RESOURCEbase64>` attributes MUST NOT be serialized as HTTP headers, even if their values can be considered "scalar", because their values will appear in the HTTP body.

review.note: Response encoding excludes the singular Document and base64 fields before considering scalar types, so even scalar JSON content cannot leak into a duplicate metadata header. Their payload remains in the HTTP body.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document / Serializing Resource Domain-Specific Documents

requirements.text: Top-level map attributes whose values are of scalar types SHOULD also appear as HTTP headers (each key having its own HTTP header) and in those cases the HTTP header names will be of the form: `xRegistry-<MAPNAME>.<KEYNAME>`. Note that map keys MAY contain the `.` character, so any `.` after the `<MAPNAME>.` is part of the key name. See [HTTP Header Values](#http-header-values) for additional information and [`labels`](#labels-attribute) for an example of one such attribute.

review.note: Scalar-valued maps emit one field per member and decode only the first dot as the map separator. Remaining dots and percent signs belong to the key, not a path or second decoding pass. Named conditional maps take precedence over active wildcards.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document / Serializing Resource Domain-Specific Documents

requirements.text: Complex top-level attributes (e.g. arrays, objects, non-scalar maps) MUST NOT appear as HTTP headers.

review.note: Complex response arrays/objects/non-scalar maps are omitted; attempts to send their values as request headers fail before dispatch. A null deletion sentinel is not a serialized complex value. An any-typed object does not become a JSON string header.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document / Serializing Resource Domain-Specific Documents

requirements.text: On update requests, similar serialization rules apply. However, rather than these headers being REQUIRED, the client would only need to include those top-level attributes that they would like to change. But, including unchanged attributes MAY be done. Unless otherwise stated, any attributes not included in request messages MUST be interpreted as a request to leave their values unchanged. Using a value of `null` (case-sensitive) MUST be processed as a request to delete that attribute.

review.note: Document header writes preserve omitted metadata, allow unchanged writable discriminator context and interpret exactly lowercase decoded null as deletion. Null, empty and absent are distinct. A literal request string null requires $details; quoting or percent-encoding does not invent an escape from the frozen sentinel.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document / Serializing Resource Domain-Specific Documents

requirements.text: Any top-level map attributes that appear as HTTP headers MUST be included in their entirety and any missing keys MUST be interpreted as a request to delete those keys from the map.

review.note: The codec assembles supplied map members into one complete map, and Merge replaces the old map even though other Document metadata is patch-like. Actual HTTP assertions prove old map keys disappear while supplied empty-string values persist.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document / Serializing Resource Domain-Specific Documents

requirements.text: Since only some types of attributes can appear as HTTP headers, in order to manage the full set of attributes, the xRegistry metadata view (via use of the `$details` URL suffix) MUST be used instead.

review.note: $details plus SendAsync remains the full-metadata route. Literal null strings, empty maps, non-string any values and complex values are explicitly directed there, without synthetic escaping, default context, extra GETs or replay. Missing conditional context is a named error, not evidence that conditional scalars/maps are unsupported.

review.note: Registry-based discovery is .xregistry below the configured root, distinct from explicitly selected host /.well-known/xregistry. Both actual client destinations are asserted; unavailable registry discovery does not trigger a hidden host probe, and advertisements do not authorize fetching peers.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters

requirements.text: The [core xRegistry specification](./spec.md) defines a set of [request flags](./spec.md#request-flags) that MAY be used to control the processing of requests as well as influence how response messages are generated. Each flag is mapped to an HTTP query parameter per the following rules:

review.note: Introduces HTTP serialization of Core flags. The following records separately evaluate null flags, singleton parameters, repeated values and the filter/ignore/inline/sort exceptions; no aggregate test count is used to close them.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters

requirements.text: - When the flag is a boolean type of flag then it MUST be serialized as `?FLAG_NAME`, all lower case.

review.note: Client query pairs with null values serialize as bare flags, distinct from an empty value's equals sign. Callers supply the specified lower-case names; the server matches known flag names case-sensitively rather than normalizing arbitrary extension keys. Actual doc/binary flags affect projection.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters

requirements.text: - When the flag has a single value associated with it, then it MUST be serialized as `?FLAG_NAME=VALUE`, where the `FLAG_NAME` MUST be all lower case. The flag MUST NOT be specified more than once.

review.note: BuildUri emits lower-case caller-supplied names with escaped =VALUE values; RequestFlags tracks recognized singletons and rejects repetitions. Existing raw tests assert valued flags and invalid values, but not duplicate singleton query rejection through the host.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters

requirements.text: - When the flag allows for multiple values, then each value MUST be serialized as a separate query parameter per the previous bullets.

review.note: The client retains ordered repeated pairs, and ParseQuery produces one entry per field instead of collapsing values. Actual wire assertions preserve repeated filter values; actual filter OR and repeated ignore tests prove the server consumes repeats with their defined exceptions.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters / `?filter` Flag

requirements.text: A server MAY support the `?filter` query parameter allowing clients to reduce the response entities to just the ones that match certain criteria.

review.note: filter is enabled and uses the shared Core QueryPlan/Evaluation over authorized logical facts before rendering. Independent raw tests assert selected IDs and typed comparisons; it is not a pass-through flag or a silent empty result for malformed supported queries.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters / `?filter` Flag

requirements.text: This query parameter MUST be serialized as:

review.note: The client URI-encodes filter values once; the host decodes one UTF-8 query pass before the Core grammar splits conjunctions. Actual requests carry escaped operators/commas and return independently expected records.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters / `?filter` Flag

requirements.text: - All `<EXPRESSION>` values within the scope of one `?filter` query parameter MUST be evaluated as a logical `AND` per the [core specification](./spec.md#filter-flag).

review.note: QueryPlan groups comma-separated expressions into one branch, and Evaluation intersects matching subtree leaves within that branch. Direct tests prove conjunction does not combine different sibling witnesses and that counts/inline results reflect the intersection.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters / `?filter` Flag

requirements.text: - The `?filter` query parameter MAY appear multiple times and if so MUST be evaluated as a logical `OR` with the other `?filter` query parameters that appear - per the [core specification](./spec.md#filter-flag).

review.note: Repeated filter parameters become separate branches whose matches are unioned in a HashSet, not ANDed or concatenated with duplicates. Selection drives child membership and URL/count projection; direct raw and subtree tests assert the resulting union independently.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters / `?ignore` Flag

requirements.text: A server MAY support the `?ignore` query parameter on any write operation to indicate that certain aspects of the request message MUST be ignored by the server.

review.note: HTTP-SEM-002 is fixed by reusing normalized owner input, not by weakening ignore or validation. Actual tests cover ignored invalid configuration, partial/unignored configuration rejection, disabled-ignore rejection, only-ignored authenticated writes, descendant denial and invalid-child atomic rollback.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters / `?ignore` Flag

requirements.text: This query parameter MUST be serialized as:

review.note: RequestFlags accepts bare ignore, empty value and '*' as the enabled ignore set, plus comma-separated named values. Direct engine cases assert each alias skips readonly entries while retaining nested identity checks; the client preserves bare versus empty wire syntax.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters / `?ignore` Flag

requirements.text: - The `?ignore` query parameter MAY be specified more than once.

review.note: Repeated ignore fields union their supported values. The actual HTTP request contains ignore=readonly and ignore=epoch and proves the unlocked Resource changes despite a stale epoch while the locked Resource is omitted and remains protected.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters / `?inline` Flag

requirements.text: A server MAY support the `?inline` query parameter on any request to indicate which nested collections/objects, or potentially large attributes, are to be included in the response message.

review.note: inline controls nested collections, meta, configuration and Document projection through ValidateInline/Includes/Child. Supported explicit inline works in actual HTTP queries. Ordinary extension objects are not falsely treated as separately inlineable entities.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters / `?inline` Flag

requirements.text: This query parameter MUST be serialized as:

review.note: The client can emit bare inline or an escaped path list; the host treats absent/empty inline value as '*' and validates model-relative paths. Actual requests exercise explicit inline paths and wildcard projection, while invalid name inlining returns the exact Core error.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters / `?inline` Flag

requirements.text: - The value portion of the `?inline` query parameter MAY Include a single `<PATH>` value or be a comma-separated list of `<PATH>` values.

review.note: RequestFlags splits a supplied inline value on commas, and projection handles each requested path with implicit collection ancestors. Actual HTTP requests assert simultaneous meta and versions.schema inlining, not just one path.

requirements.text: - The `?inline` query parameter MAY be specified more than once.

review.note: Each repeated inline field appends paths and Includes/Child evaluates their union. The inspected tests cover comma lists and generic repeated query transport, but not multiple actual inline fields selecting different branches.

requirements.text: A server MAY support the `?sort` query parameter on any request directed to a collection of Groups, Resources or Versions.

review.note: QueryPlan allows sorting only direct Group, Resource and Version collections and rejects owner sorting. Direct tests establish Group scalar ordering and Resource meta sorting; an explicit Version collection sort operation is not directly evidenced.

requirements.text: This query parameter MUST be serialized as:

Actual HTTP uses escaped rank=desc and checks returned order; direct cases cover default direction and invalid projections.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Header Values

requirements.text: Some attributes can contain arbitrary UTF-8 string content, and per [RFC7230, section 3][rfc7230-section-3], HTTP headers MUST only use printable characters from the US-ASCII character set, and are terminated by a CRLF sequence with OPTIONAL whitespace around the header value.

review.note: Header encoding produces printable ASCII; the decoder rejects unencoded controls/non-ASCII and handles optional transport whitespace. PreparedResponse validates emitted fields before publication, and Kestrel/HttpClient own HTTP CRLF framing rather than concatenating decoded attribute text into fields.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Header Values

requirements.text: When encoding an attribute's value as an HTTP header, it MUST be percent-encoded as described below. This is compatible with [RFC3986, section 2.1][rfc3986-section-2-1] but is more specific about what needs encoding. The resulting string SHOULD NOT be further encoded. (Rationale: quoted string escaping is unnecessary when every space and double-quote character is already percent-encoded.)

review.note: RegistryHeaderEncoding encodes spaces, quotes, percent and nonprintable/non-ASCII UTF-8 bytes once, with no added quoted-string layer. Literal independent HTTP assertions cover percent, controls and Unicode. Standard Content-Type retains its separate HTTP media-type syntax, as reviewed on its dedicated clause.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Header Values

requirements.text: When decoding an HTTP header into an attribute's value, any HTTP header value MUST first be unescaped with respect to double-quoted strings, as described in [RFC7230, section 3.2.6][rfc7230-section-3-2-6]. A single round of percent-decoding MUST then be performed as described below. HTTP headers for attribute values do not support parenthetical comments, so the initial unescaping only needs to handle double-quoted values, including processing backslash escapes within double-quoted values. Header values produced via the percent-encoding described here will never include double-quoted values, but they MUST be supported when receiving events, for compatibility with older versions of this specification which did not require double-quote and space characters to be percent-encoded.

review.note: Legacy quoted strings are unescaped before exactly one percent-decoding pass; backslash escapes inside quotes are handled and parentheses are not stripped as comments. Tests prove %2520 remains %20 and quoted/encoded null cannot become a request literal-string escape.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Header Values

requirements.text: Percent encoding is performed by considering each Unicode character within the attribute's canonical string representation. Any character represented in memory as a [Unicode surrogate pair][surrogate-pair] MUST be treated as a single Unicode character. The following characters MUST be percent-encoded:

review.note: Strict UTF-8 conversion treats a valid surrogate pair as one Unicode scalar before byte percent encoding; lone surrogates fail. The required character set and exact encoded-byte limits are independently asserted, including boundary-plus-one failure.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Header Values

requirements.text: Percent-encoding SHOULD be performed using upper-case for values A-F, but decoding MUST accept lowercase values.

review.note: The encoder uses a fixed uppercase hex alphabet; HexValue accepts both cases. Independent lower-case UTF-8 input vectors and an actual host request prove decoding is not accidentally uppercase-only.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Header Values

requirements.text: When performing percent-decoding, values that have been unnecessarily percent-encoded MUST be accepted, but encoded byte sequences which are invalid in UTF-8 MUST generate an error ([header_error](#header_error)). For example, "%C0%A0" is an overlong encoding of U+0020, and would be rejected.

review.note: Unnecessary valid escapes are decoded, but strict UTF-8 rejects overlong, surrogate, out-of-range and truncated sequences. The host converts codec errors into the HTTP header_error catalog with the actual header name and rejects publication.

review.note: The two source-proven diagnostics defects HTTP-SEM-003/004 are fixed with direct mounted-HTTP, required-null/default/missing and rollback tests. The catalog still supplies standard type/title/subject/args and explicit extension errors. This broad whole-section record remains pending a complete per-error/output matrix rather than treating fixes to those two defects as proof of every surrounding error definition.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Error Processing / api_not_found

requirements.text: `request_path` MUST be the "Path" portion of the incoming request URL, starting with `/`. E.g. `/export` if the "export" feature is not supported.

review.note: HTTP-SEM-004 is fixed and directly verified. HTTP request_path definitions use the incoming escaped URL path with PathBase and MountPath intact, excluding its query. api_not_found, missing_body, extra_xregistry_header, header_error and engine-origin missing_versions all cross the real mounted Kestrel seam. Core XID subjects and details_required remain Registry-relative; no blanket prefixing or query disclosure is introduced.

review.note: This subsection describes the attribute-map key, not an additional string-valued definition object. CompileAttributes consumes that key, checks its grammar, and fills Name; tests assert an inferred effective name and reject a contradictory explicit name.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.name`

requirements.text: - REQUIRED.

review.note: Effective attribute definitions always contain name. Source shorthand/omitted name is normalized from the owning key rather than requiring redundant source text, consistent with the source/effective distinction and abbreviated examples; the effective name is directly asserted.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.name`

requirements.text: - The name of the attribute. MUST be the same as its key in the owning `attributes` map. A value of `*` indicates support for undefined extension names at runtime. Absence of a `*` attribute indicates lack of support for undefined extensions the presence of an unknown attribute at runtime MUST generate an ([unknown_attribute](./spec.md#unknown_attribute)) error.

review.note: The compiler/validator implement this explicit model-admission rule, and the engine test asserts unknown_attribute with no publication for an undeclared field without a wildcard. Core's notations also say server-unknown extensions MUST be stored, but qualify acceptance with a bad-state exception. Cross-reading reveals a wording ambiguity, not a proven unconditional contradiction or a demonstrated runtime defect; the broader storage interpretation remains unresolved.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.name`

requirements.text: Often `*` is used with a `type` of `any` to allow for any undefined extension name of any supported data type. By default, the model does not support undefined extensions. Note that undefined extensions, if supported, MUST adhere to the same rules as [defined extensions](./spec.md#attributes-and-extensions).

review.note: The default model does not insert an ordinary wildcard. An explicit wildcard admits otherwise unnamed fields subject to names/types; an enclosing any instead preserves opaque valid JSON without modeling its descendants. These admission mechanisms must not be confused with bespoke server knowledge of an extension's meaning. The related notational storage ambiguity and direct opaque persistence evidence remain open.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.name`

requirements.text: An attribute of `*` MUST NOT use the `ifvalues` feature, but a non-`*` attribute MAY define an `ifvalues` attribute named `*` as long as there isn't already one defined for this level in the entity.

review.note: RejectsInvalidModelAspectsWithExactPointers checks that * cannot define ifvalues and that a conditional * conflicts with a static *. ConditionalWildcardNeverOverridesDeclaredAttributes verifies that declared attributes still take precedence.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.name`

requirements.text: An extension attribute MUST NOT use a name that conflicts with any specification-defined attribute, sub-object attribute or collection-related attribute names defined at the same level in the hierarchy. For Resource/Version attributes, this applies for both levels - e.g. a Version-level extension MUST NOT use a name that conflicts with its Resource-level attribute names.

review.note: Compiler-owned MODEL-REV-002 is resolved: Resource projection names cannot be declared as Version extensions in static definitions or recursively nested ifvalues sibling maps, even in inactive branches. Nested object and collection-item scopes remain independent. Metadata-only document-name handling belongs to the parent's separate MODEL-REV-007 work and is not qualified by this recovery. RESOLVED MODEL-REV-007: Document-form names are special only for document-bearing Resources. Explicitly modeled or wildcard-admitted metadata-only extensions using those names survive write/read/PATCH without decoding or URL acquisition; unmodeled forms and actual Document streams still reject.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.type`

requirements.text: - REQUIRED.

review.note: RejectsInvalidModelAspectsWithExactPointers verifies that a new attribute without type fails with model_error at its type member.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.type`

requirements.text: - The "TYPE" of the attribute being defined. MUST be one of the data types (in lower case) defined in [Attributes and Extensions](./spec.md#attributes-and-extensions).

review.note: ModelTypes.Parse uses exact lowercase names for the prose-defined types and rejects uppercase STRING. Binary is deliberately rejected: it appears in derived artifacts but not the referenced normative data-type list. Exact numeric types are not narrowed to CLR integer/double ranges.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.target`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

review.note: XID and URI/URL definitions compile without target. Targetless XIDs remain unrestricted by model type; slash-relative URI/URL values remain unconstrained when target is absent.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.target`

requirements.text: - The type of entity that this attribute points to when `type` is set to `url`, `uri` or `xid`. `target` MUST NOT be used for any other type of attribute.

review.note: CompileAttribute restricts target to xid, uri and url, not their absolute/relative variants. Direct invalid string and urlabsolute definitions verify rejection at /target; the URI template-shape rejection is also asserted.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.target`

requirements.text: - The value of this model attribute MUST be an "xid template" of one of the following forms:

review.note: RESOLVED MODEL-REV-009: Resource-only and optional-Version XID targets now require the corresponding positive entity kinds and reject Meta. Valid dangling Resource/Version IDs remain allowed with explicit model context; targetless XIDs and absent-context obligations retain their separate contracts. The compound clause remains pending its other direct-evidence obligations.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.target`

requirements.text: - `/<GROUPS>` - a plural Group type name. An entity attribute of this type/target MUST reference an instance of this Group type.

review.note: CheckTarget resolves `/gs` to Group plural `gs` and rejects Resources or Versions below it. DeclaredTargetsAcceptDanglingEntityIdsWithoutExistenceChecks accepts a dangling Group ID; TargetsRejectTheWrongEntityKindOrDeclaredModelType rejects both a Resource path and a Group ID under another plural.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.target`

requirements.text: - `/<GROUPS>/<RESOURCES>` - a plural Resource type name. An entity attribute of this type/target MUST reference an instance of this Resource type, not a specific Version of the Resource.

review.note: RESOLVED MODEL-REV-009: Resource-only and optional-Version XID targets now require the corresponding positive entity kinds and reject Meta. Valid dangling Resource/Version IDs remain allowed with explicit model context; targetless XIDs and absent-context obligations retain their separate contracts.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.target`

requirements.text: - `/<GROUPS>/<RESOURCES>[/versions]`. An entity attribute of this type/target MUST reference either an instance of this Resource type or an instance of a Version of this Resource type. Note the `[/versions]` portion of the `target` value is that exact string, including the square brackets.

review.note: RESOLVED MODEL-REV-009: Resource-only and optional-Version XID targets now require the corresponding positive entity kinds and reject Meta. Valid dangling Resource/Version IDs remain allowed with explicit model context; targetless XIDs and absent-context obligations retain their separate contracts.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.target`

requirements.text: - `/GROUPS/<RESOURCES>/versions` - a Version of a Resource type. An entity attribute of this type/target MUST reference an instance of a Version of this Resource type, not the Resource itself.

review.note: The `/versions` target requires a Version of the declared Resource type. DeclaredTargetsAcceptDanglingEntityIdsWithoutExistenceChecks accepts a dangling Version ID; TargetsRejectTheWrongEntityKindOrDeclaredModelType rejects a Resource and a Meta path.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.target`

requirements.text: - An `xid` entity attribute that includes a `target` value as part of its model definition MUST match the `target` entity type specified. An `xid` attribute that does not include a `target` definition has no such restriction and MAY be any valid `xid` value.

review.note: RESOLVED MODEL-REV-009: Resource-only and optional-Version XID targets now require the corresponding positive entity kinds and reject Meta. Valid dangling Resource/Version IDs remain allowed with explicit model context; targetless XIDs and absent-context obligations retain their separate contracts.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.target`

requirements.text: - A URI/URL entity attribute MAY include `target` as part of its definition. If so, then any runtime value that is a relative URI/URL (begins with `/`) MUST be an `xid` and MUST adhere to the `target` entity type specified, if specified. Absolute URIs/URLs are not constrained by the presence of a `target` value.

review.note: Slash-rooted URI/URL values with a declared target are parsed as XIDs and checked against the effective model and target type. Absolute and non-slash-relative values bypass target constraints; valid slash-rooted values retain the explicit host policy obligation.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.namecharset`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL, and MUST only be used when `type` is `object`.

review.note: Namecharset is optional for objects, while a non-null namecharset on a scalar is rejected even when its value is strict. The exact-path invalid-aspect test exercises this restriction; nested extended-object compilation exercises the allowed form.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.namecharset`

requirements.text: - Specifies the name of the character set that defines the allowable characters that can be used for the object's top-level attribute names. Any attempt to define a top-level attribute for this object that does not adhere to the characters defined by the character set name MUST generate an error ([invalid_attribute](./spec.md#invalid_attribute)).

review.note: Runtime tests reject a dashed name under strict and an uppercase name under extended with invalid_attribute; valid extended punctuation and digit-leading names are accepted.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.namecharset`

requirements.text: - Per the [Attributes and Extensions](./spec.md#attributes-and-extensions) section, attribute names are normally limited to just the set of characters that ensure they can reliably be used in cases such as code variable names without the need for some escaping mechanism. However, there are situations where object-typed attribute names need to support additional characters, such as a dash (`-`), and it is known that they will never be used in those restricted character set situations. By setting the `namecharset` aspect to `extended` the server MUST allow for an extended set of valid characters in attribute names for this object.

review.note: Runtime tests accept digit-leading names and names containing dash, dot, or colon under extended naming; they reject uppercase names.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.namecharset`

requirements.text: The allowed character set for attribute names within an `object` MUST also apply to the top-level `siblingattributes` of any `ifvalues` defined for those attributes.

review.note: An executable model test accepts and validates a dashed conditional sibling under extended object naming, then confirms the same definition is rejected under strict naming.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.namecharset`

requirements.text: - When not specified, the default value MUST be `strict`.

review.note: A direct test confirms omitted namecharset compiles and serializes as strict, accepts a valid name, and rejects a dashed name at runtime.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.namecharset`

requirements.text: - The value of this attribute MUST be case-insensitive.

review.note: Namecharset is canonicalized with ToLowerInvariant before supported-value checks. The direct EXTENDED case asserts the compiled value is extended and accepts its dashed child name.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.namecharset`

requirements.text: - Implementations MAY define additional character sets, however, an attempt to define a model that uses an unknown character set name MUST generate an error ([model_error](./spec.md#model_error)). There is currently no mechanism defined by this specification to discover the list (or definition) of additional `namecharset` values supported by an implementation. Implementations SHOULD use their documentation to advertise this extension.

review.note: This implementation chooses only strict and extended; extra character sets are permitted, not mandatory. Unknown sets produce the required model_error with a direct exact-path assertion. The documentation recommendation for advertising implementation-defined sets is inapplicable because none are added.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.description`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

review.note: Attribute descriptions are optional strings and survive compilation. The include precedence test asserts that the earlier included description is retained, independently of the type check and the local sibling's overriding definition.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.enum`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

review.note: Enum is optional; omitted enum leaves an empty immutable list and allows otherwise valid values. The scalar metadata cases directly accept values on definitions without enum, without coercing their JSON kinds.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.enum`

requirements.text: - A list of possible values for this attribute. Each item in the array MUST be of the type defined by `type`. When not specified, or an empty array, there are no restrictions on the value set of this attribute. This MUST only be used when the `type` is a scalar. See the `strict` attribute below.

review.note: An empty enum imposes no value restriction, but the declared scalar type still applies; the dedicated test accepts an out-of-enum string and rejects a number.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.enum`

requirements.text: When specified without `strict` being `true`, this list is just a suggested set of values and the attribute is NOT REQUIRED to use one of them.

review.note: A direct scalar test accepts a string outside the enum when strict is false and still rejects a nonstring value.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.strict`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

review.note: Strict is an optional Boolean with a true baseline. Omitting it while supplying enum/default is exercised by the exact model_error for a default outside the enum, so omission does not accidentally disable strictness.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.strict`

requirements.text: - Indicates whether the attribute restricts its values to just the array of values specified in `enum` or not. A value of `true` means that any values used that are not part of the `enum` set MUST generate an error ([invalid_attribute](./spec.md#invalid_attribute)). This attribute has no impact when `enum` is absent or an empty array.

review.note: RESOLVED MODEL-REV-013: Timestamp enum comparison uses normalized instants without discarding arbitrary fractional precision, so validated output/defaults remain valid on subsequent completion. The shared Group constraint enum/equals path now uses the same typed instant comparison; adjacent nanoseconds reject and ordinary strings remain ordinal.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.strict`

requirements.text: - When not specified, the default value MUST be `true`.

review.note: A direct model test omits strict on an enum-bearing attribute and asserts true in both the compiled model and effective-model output.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.matchversions`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

review.note: The direct default test compiles a Resource attribute with matchversions omitted and confirms that omission is accepted.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.matchversions`

requirements.text: - Indicates whether all Versions of a Resource instance MUST have the same value for this attribute (or MUST be missing from all Versions). If an inconsistency is found then an error ([mismatched_version_attribute](spec.md#mismatched_version_attribute)) MUST be generated.

review.note: RESOLVED MODEL-REV-012: Cross-Version matching checks actual derived default membership after final ordering/retention rather than stored false placeholders. A single retained Version remains valid; model updates introducing an inconsistent equality rule reject as model_compliance_error. The compound clause remains pending its other direct-evidence obligations.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.matchversions`

requirements.text: - This aspect MUST only be `true` for attribute definitions that:

review.note: Tests reject matchversions on object, array, map, wildcard, conditional, array-item, and map-item definitions; a static scalar nested object attribute is accepted.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.matchversions`

requirements.text: - When not specified, the default value MUST be `false`.

review.note: A direct model test omits matchversions on a Resource attribute and asserts false in both the compiled model and effective-model output.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.readonly`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

review.note: Readonly is optional. The compiler preserves explicit true, while ordinary attributes remain writable; ClientInput validation distinguishes both within the same request and preserves a writable null deletion instead of supplying its default.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.readonly`

requirements.text: - Indicates whether this attribute is modifiable by a client. Unless otherwise stated, during creation, or update, of an entity if this attribute is specified, then its value MUST be silently ignored by the server even if the value is invalid. Note that there are some readonly attributes that are examined by a server during a write operation (e.g. `epoch` and IDs).

review.note: RESOLVED MODEL-REV-001: Retained top-level PATCH discriminator context is explicitly supplied to ClientInput validation. Submitted discriminator changes/null, readonly values, nested object replacement, defaults and subsequent complete validation retain their original rules. No HTTP prefetch or implicit partial-header context is introduced.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.readonly`

requirements.text: - When not specified, the default value MUST be `false`.

review.note: An extension's omitted readonly falls back to false. The submitted-metadata test observes a non-readonly count:null surviving beside a discarded readonly field, rather than silently ignoring both attributes.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.readonly`

requirements.text: - When the attribute name is `*` then `readonly` MUST NOT be set to `true`.

review.note: CompileAttribute rejects readonly:true on *, including before runtime wildcard lookup. The exact model-aspect table directly expects model_error at /attributes/* for this input.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.immutable`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

review.note: A direct model test omits immutable on an extension attribute and confirms the aspect is accepted.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.immutable`

requirements.text: - Indicates whether this attribute's value can be changed once it is set. This MUST ONLY be used for server-controlled specification-defined attributes, such as `specversion` and `<SINGULAR>id`, and MUST NOT be used for extension attributes. As such, it is only for informational purposes for clients.

review.note: The compiler rejects immutable on extension attributes; tests also verify inherited system immutable flags survive model compilation and appear in effective-model output.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.immutable`

requirements.text: Once set, any attempt to update the value MUST be silently ignored by the server.

review.note: A non-readonly immutable value is retained across changed and null PATCH values and across a replacement that omits it; other writable fields in those operations still change.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.immutable`

requirements.text: - When not specified, the default value MUST be `false`.

review.note: A direct model test asserts immutable is false in both the compiled model and effective-model output when omitted.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.required`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

review.note: Required is optional but a supplied value must be Boolean. The aspect test rejects the string true, and the optional-parent test proves omission of an ordinary object is allowed despite required/defaulted children inside it.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.required`

requirements.text: - Indicates whether this attribute is REQUIRED to have a non-null value.

review.note: CompleteEntity requires a non-null value after defaults/conditionals. Current direct assertions reject explicit deletion of existing required values at top level, in nested objects and collection items, and on Versions; the Document-header case also verifies stored bytes/epoch survive. A defined default still restores a non-null value.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.required`

requirements.text: - When set to `true`, this specification does not mandate how this attribute's value is populated (i.e. by a client, the server or via a default value), just that by the end of the server's processing of any request it MUST have a non-null value, and generate an error ([invalid_attribute](./spec.md#invalid_attribute)) if not. Note that this implies that a REQUIRED attribute does not mean that clients are mandated to include that attribute in their requests. If the attribute will automatically be populated by the server (e.g. it has a default value defined) the client MAY omit it.

review.note: Core model.md:374-382 requires invalid_attribute when a required value remains null. Core HTTP Binding http.md:232-235 and 253-255 requires required_attribute_missing for the same condition after PUT/PATCH. Current HTTP behavior and tests follow the binding clause; this model requirement remains pending until the conflicting MUSTs are resolved. Implicit-parent creation separately requires required_attribute_missing.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.required`

requirements.text: - A `true` value also implies that this attribute MUST be serialized in any response from the server - with the exception of the optimizations specified for [document view](./spec.md#registry-model).

review.note: Completed metadata retains required/defaulted values, and normal render paths clone them; document view intentionally omits the Resource's default-Version projection. Tests separately assert a populated default and the document-view omission, but do not enumerate every required attribute across all server response shapes.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.required`

requirements.text: - When not specified the default value MUST be `false`.

review.note: Required defaults false for new definitions. The optional-parent test successfully omits an object whose own required aspect is absent; required child/default processing occurs only when that object exists.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.required`

requirements.text: - When the attribute name is `*` then `required` MUST NOT be set to `true`.

review.note: Required:true on * is rejected by the dedicated wildcard aspect guard. The exact-path model table directly asserts model_error for that prohibited combination.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.required`

requirements.text: - When a default value (`attributes.<STRING>.default`) is defined, then this aspect MUST be `true`, otherwise an error ([model_required_true](./spec.md#model_required_true)) MUST be generated.

review.note: A non-null default requires required:true; omission of required does not silently promote it. Core asserts model_required_true at the required pointer, and the engine contract test preserves the model-specific error and attribute name without publishing.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.default`

requirements.text: - Type: MUST be a non-`null` value of the type specified by the `attributes.<STRING>.type` model attribute and MUST only be used for scalar types. Attempts to define a `default` value for a non-scalar type MUST generate an error ([model_scalar_default](./spec.md#model_scalar_default)).

review.note: Non-null defaults are restricted to scalar types and checked without numeric narrowing; nonscalar defaults yield model_scalar_default. The later null/absence paragraph is honored: explicit default:null means no default, not a stored null default. Tests cover nonscalar, fractional integer and large exact defaults.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.default`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

review.note: A default may be absent; explicit null is also absence in the compiled definition while the original Source keeps the explicit null. The ownership/presence test checks both representations rather than equating null with an empty string or zero.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.default`

requirements.text: - This value MUST be used to populate this attribute's value if one was not provided by a client. An attribute with a default value does not mean that its owning Object is mandated to be present; rather the attribute would only appear when the owning Object is present. By default, attributes have no default values.

review.note: Validator.Object inserts defaults only in completed, present objects and before required checks/conditional activation. Core tests distinguish an omitted optional parent from present empty/null-child cases. The current server test additionally null-resets existing top-level/nested required values and directly observes fallback after the diagnostic fix.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.default`

requirements.text: - When a default value is specified, this attribute MUST be serialized in responses from servers as part of its owning entity, even if it is set to its default value. This means that any attribute that has a default value defined MUST also have its `required` aspect set to `true`.

review.note: Defaulted attributes must be required in the model and remain explicit values in normalized metadata. Tests read back the actual default, including a Group-constraint-supplied value from an engine response; this is not inferred from a successful compile alone.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.default`

requirements.text: - If the default value of an attribute changes over time, all existing instances of that attribute MUST retain their current values and not be automatically changed to the new default value. In other words, a new default value MUST only apply to new or subsequent updates (when set to `null`, which would reset it to the current default value) of existing instances of the attribute.

review.note: An engine test changes a default from red to blue, verifies an existing value stays red and a new entity receives blue, then resets the old value with null and checks blue survives restart.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.default`

requirements.text: - If the attribute is defined to have an `enum` list, and its `strict` aspect is `true`, then if a `default` value is specified it MUST be one of those `enum` values.

review.note: After reading enum/default, CompileAttribute checks the effective default with Allowed. The direct string c versus enum [a,b] case fails, and the shared exact scalar comparator avoids floating-point equivalence errors for numeric values.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.attributes`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

review.note: A direct test compiles object attributes both without a nested attribute map and with an empty map.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.attributes`

requirements.text: - MAY be present when the owning attribute's `type` is `object`, otherwise it MUST NOT be present. It MAY be absent or an empty list if there are no defined attributes for the nested `object`.

review.note: A direct test accepts nested attributes both when omitted and when supplied as an empty map, and verifies both compile to an empty attribute definition; the exact-path model test rejects the aspect on a string.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.item`

requirements.text: - REQUIRED when owning attribute's `type` is `map` or `array`.

review.note: Array/map definitions require an item unless inheriting a system item's existing definition. The direct missing-array-item rejection and nested array/map/object compilation exercise rejection and successful item structure.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.item`

requirements.text: - Defines the nested entity that this attribute references. This attribute MUST only be used when the owning attribute's `type` value is `map` or `array`.

review.note: Item describes the nested array element or map value; a string-typed owner with item is rejected at /item. The compiled nested array-of-map-of-object test observes the ultimate x:string definition rather than merely successful parsing.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.item.type`

requirements.text: - REQUIRED.

review.note: RejectsInvalidModelAspectsWithExactPointers verifies that an array item without type fails at /attributes/a/item/type. CompilesNestedItemsAndStaticVersionMatchObligations verifies nested item types.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.item.target`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL, and MUST only be used when `item.type` is `url`, `uri` or `xid`.

review.note: RESOLVED MODEL-REV-009: Resource-only and optional-Version XID targets now require the corresponding positive entity kinds and reject Meta. Valid dangling Resource/Version IDs remain allowed with explicit model context; targetless XIDs and absent-context obligations retain their separate contracts. The compound clause remains pending its other direct-evidence obligations.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.item.namecharset`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL, and MUST only be used when `item.type` is `object`.

review.note: A direct test accepts an extended dashed name on an object item and rejects namecharset on a scalar item.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.maxversions`

requirements.text: - A value of zero (`0`) indicates there is no stated limit, and implementations MAY prune non-default Versions at any time. This means it is valid for an implementation to only support one (`1`) Version when `maxversions` is set to `0`.

review.note: Zero means no stated retention limit, not infinite resource budgets and not a mandated minimum history. This engine chooses no automatic count pruning at zero; the two-Version sticky/default test uses an omitted limit. The specification's permission to retain only one is not an implementation requirement.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.maxversions`

requirements.text: - When the limit is exceeded, implementations MUST prune Versions by deleting the oldest Version first (based on the Resource's [`versionmode`](#groupsstringresourcesstringversionmode) algorithm), skipping the Version marked as "default". Once the single oldest Version is determined, delete it. A special case for the pruning rules is that if `maxversions` is set to one (1), then the "default" Version is not skipped, which means it will be deleted and the new Version will become "default".

review.note: FinalizeResource orders/prunes one Version at a time, rebuilding ancestry; it skips the selected default except at limit one. RetentionSkipsStickyDefaultUsingEachVersionModeOrdering covers all four modes, including timestamp ties, while RetentionBoundariesPreserveExactNewestChainAcrossVersionModes proves limits zero, one, two and omitted across the modes, including limit-one replacement of the prior default.

See [`defaultversionsticky` Attribute](spec.md#defaultversionsticky-attribute) for additional information.

ReducingMaxVersionsToOneRejectsAnyStickyResourceAtomically tests either of two existing Resources as sticky, asserts the error and unchanged persistence generation, model, export and events, then clears stickiness and verifies successful pruning.

requirements.text: - Regardless of the algorithm used, implementations MUST ensure that the `ancestorid` attribute of all Versions of a Resource accurately represents the relationship of the Versions prior to the completion of any operation. Similarly, the `defaultversionid` of the Resource might change if its `defaultversionsticky` attribute is `false`.

The modifiedat fixed-point test asserts exact final ancestors/default, and timestamp-ordering tests cover insertion order differences. source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.versionmode`

requirements.text: - `manual` - Newest Version: MUST be determined by finding all Versions that are not referenced as an `ancestor` of another Version, then finding the one with the newest `createdat` timestamp. If there is more than one, then the one with the highest alphabetically case-insensitive `versionid` value MUST be chosen. - Oldest Version: MUST be determined by finding all root Versions (ones that have an `ancestorid` value that points to itself), then finding the one with the oldest `createdat` timestamp. If there is more than one, then the one with the lowest alphabetically case-insensitive `versionid` MUST be chosen. - Ancestor Processing: typically provided by clients. During a "create" operation, all new Versions that do not have an `ancestorid` value provided MUST be sorted/processed by `versionid` (in case-insensitive ascending order) and the `ancestorid` value of each MUST be set to the current "newest Version" per the above semantics. Note that as each new Version is created, it MUST become the "newest". If there is no existing Version then the new Version becomes a root and its `ancestorid` value MUST be its own `versionid` attribute value. - Deleted Ancestor: if a Version's ancestor is deleted, then this Version MUST become a root, and its `ancestorid` value MUST be set to its own `versionid` value. - The name of this versionmode is a bit of a misnomer in that it is not 100% "manual". As stated above, as a convenience, by default new Versions will point to the "newest" Version as their ancestor. If this behavior is not desired, then during the "create" operation, the `ancestorid` can be set to point to itself (or any other Version) if desired.

review.note: All manual subclauses were read: newest leaf, oldest root, createdat/ID ties, sorted implicit creations, self-root initialization and reroot after deletion. Source implements these paths using ordinal-ignore-case ID ordering. Tests prove ordinary chains/deletion, not multi-root backdated batches or every tie/pruning case.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.versionmode`

requirements.text: - `createdat` - Newest Version: MUST be determined by finding the Version with the newest `createdat` timestamp. If there is more than one, then the one with the highest alphabetically case-insensitive `versionid` value MUST be chosen. - Oldest Version: MUST be determined by finding the Version with the oldest `createdat` timestamp. If there is more than one, then the one with the lowest alphabetically case-insensitive `versionid` value MUST be chosen. Note that this MUST also be the one and only "root" Version. - Ancestor Processing: The `ancestorid` value of each Version MUST be determined via examination of the `createdat` timestamp of each Version and the Versions sorted in ascending order, where the first one will be the "root" (oldest) Version and its `ancestorid` value MUST be its `versionid`. If there is more than one Version with the same `createdat` timestamp then those MUST be ordered in ascending case-insensitive order based on their `versionid` values. - Deleted Ancestor: if a Version's ancestor is deleted, then this Version's `ancestorid` value MUST be determined by the "ancestor processing" logic as stated above. - When this `versionmode` is used, the `singleversionroot` aspect MUST be set to `true`.

review.note: Createdat ordering builds a single sorted chain, self-points the oldest root and chooses the last Version as newest, using exact normalized timestamp fractions and ID ties. Direct tests assert out-of-order creation and equivalent zero-fraction ties; mode-specific deletion and lower/high ID tie matrices remain unasserted.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.versionmode`

requirements.text: - `modifiedat` - This is the same as the `createdat` algorithm except that the `modifiedat` attribute of each Version MUST be used instead of the `createdat` attribute.

review.note: Modifiedat reuses timestamp ordering with the modifiedat field, including repeated repair because ancestry changes themselves touch timestamps. The fixed-point test asserts the exact stable chain after an edit; inherited createdat algorithm obligations such as mode-specific deletion/ties are not all directly tested.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.versionmode`

requirements.text: - `semver` - Newest Version: MUST be the Version with the highest `versionid` value per the [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/) specification's "precedence" ordering rules. - Oldest Version: MUST be the Version with the lowest `versionid` value per the [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/) specification's "precedence" ordering rules. Note that this MUST also be the one and only "root" Version. - Ancestor Processing: The `ancestorid` value of each Version MUST either be its `versionid` value (if it is the oldest Version), or the `versionid` of the next oldest Version per the [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/) specification's "precedence" ordering rules. - Deleted Ancestor: if a Version's ancestor is deleted, then this Version's `ancestorid` value MUST be determined by the "ancestor processing" logic as stated above. - When this `versionmode` is used, the `singleversionroot` aspect MUST be set to `true`.

review.note: SemanticVersion parses exact numeric components, rejects leading-zero numeric prereleases, applies numeric-versus-text prerelease precedence, and ignores build metadata for precedence. Engine ordering builds a single chain. The direct 1.0.0-rc.1/2.0.0 case is not the full precedence, invalid-ID and deletion matrix.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.typemap`

requirements.text: If more than one entry in the `typemap` matches the `contenttype`, but they all have the same value, then that value MUST be used. If they are not all the same, then `binary` MUST be used.

review.note: Lookup examines every matching entry: equal results are retained and any conflicting result becomes Binary, without most-specific-pattern precedence. The direct text/plain case has agreeing implicit/wildcard matches; text/mine has conflicting string/json matches and resolves Binary.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.typemap`

requirements.text: - The key MAY include at most one `*` to act as a wildcard to mean zero or more instances of any character at that position in the string - similar to a `.*` in a regular expression. The key MUST be a case-insensitive string.

review.note: The compiler rejects more than one star; lookup implements prefix/suffix matching with zero-or-more middle characters and ordinal-ignore-case comparisons. Direct repeated-star rejection and ordinary wildcard/case matches exist, but no direct zero-character wildcard match is asserted.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.typemap`

requirements.text: Implementations MAY define additional values.

review.note: Additional typemap result values are permitted but not mandatory. This implementation deliberately limits the set to binary, json and string. The preceding value definitions were read; declining to add yaml or another extension is not missing required behavior.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.typemap`

requirements.text: A value of `json` indicates that the Resource's document is JSON and MUST be serialized under the `<RESOURCE>` attribute if it is valid JSON. Note that if there is a syntax error in the JSON then the server MUST treat the document as `binary` to avoid sending invalid JSON to the client. The server MAY choose to modify the formatting of the document (e.g. to "pretty-print" it).

review.note: InlineDocument parses json-mapped bytes into the Resource attribute and falls back to exact base64 for invalid_json, invalid_utf8 or duplicate_member. Tests assert valid JSON structure and invalid UTF-8 fallback. A genuine malformed JSON-text case and other strict parser rejection categories are not directly asserted.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.typemap`

requirements.text: Specifying an unknown (or unsupported) value MUST generate an error ([model_error](./spec.md#model_error)) during the update of the xRegistry model.

review.note: Unknown typemap values fail compilation through the supported-value switch. The direct yaml input expects model_error at its typemap entry, rather than silently defaulting an unsupported requested mapping to binary.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.typemap`

requirements.text: By default, the following [RFC9110](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9110#media.type) `typemap` keys MUST be implicitly defined as follows, unless overridden by an explicit `typemap` entry:

review.note: The implicit application/json, *+json and text/plain mappings are installed before explicit entries. Direct tests observe all three and an explicit case-insensitive Application/JSON override to binary; no absent mapping is treated as JSON by guesswork.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.attributes`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

review.note: Version extension attributes are optional; omitted lists are populated with the Version system baseline and conditional Document fields. The minimal model directly observes required versionid, and hasdocument:false tests confirm Document definitions are absent rather than merely hidden in output.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.attributes`

requirements.text: - Extension attribute names at this level MUST NOT overlap with extension attributes defined at the `groups.resources.resourceattributes` level. The only duplicate names allowed are specification-defined attributes such as `self` and `xid`, and the Version-specific values MUST be overridden by the Resource-level values when serialized.

review.note: The compiler-owned named-extension uniqueness gap is resolved: conditional Version siblings are recursively checked against Resource projection reservations, with independent nested object/item scopes preserved. Normal Resource projection and Server serialization remain separate obligations whose qualification is not inferred from these Core runs.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.resourceattributes`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

review.note: Resourceattributes is optional because the compiler supplies Resource navigation fields separately from Version attributes and Meta attributes. Runtime alias projection asserts Resource self/ID while preserving target Version metadata, but no direct complete effective ResourceAttributes enumeration exists.
