Pending is not a blanket missing-runtime claim: the cited local behavior is distinguished from the stated source duty, optional workflow, external policy or aggregate qualification. Duty classification: deployment-operator-duty. Current source/assertion evidence is not automatic native/all-platform or aggregate release qualification; historical proposal and receipts remain preserved.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Notations and Terminology

requirements.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119).

review.note: RFC2119 terminology is not an independent operation. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Notations and Terminology

requirements.text: The catalog's `registryid`, its entry's `registryid` and the described Registry root's `registryid` have different scopes. Their values need not match. A catalog-description `versionid`, target Resource `versionid`, OCI digest, Git commit and endpoint address MUST NOT be treated as interchangeable.

review.note: Catalog selection keeps the description Version separate from the catalog context and the target content Version; immutable origin data never enters Core metadata. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Hosting Models / API Server Resolution

requirements.text: A conforming server-hosted resolver MUST expose a Core-conforming Registry through each consumer-facing binding that it implements. Its model MUST describe the resulting view. Responses, including source-derived data, MUST use the consumer-facing Registry's identity and navigation according to that binding. Source provenance and revision information remain separate.

review.note: The producer frontend materializes consumer identity/navigation and publishes its own model. Full-model projection constraints and write-validation controls are undergoing the separate Producer completion gate; this row is not promoted from simple projections. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Hosting Models / API Server Resolution

requirements.text: The server MUST apply the source-selection, shadowing, error and completeness rules below. It MUST NOT expose unrelated source identities as though their XIDs were globally interchangeable. The server's advertised capabilities describe what it can provide, not the union of features advertised by sources.

review.note: Resource-level precedence and failure semantics have direct evidence. The complete producer capabilities/model/count contract remains with the separate Producer completion gate. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Hosting Models / API Server Resolution

requirements.text: The server MUST signal `producer` resolution for this consumer-facing view as specified below. Its clients read the server's results directly instead of repeating the server's catalog traversal.

review.note: Enabled-owner parsing and direct producer reads are implemented. The consumer-facing producer advertisement and complete frontend behavior are not inferred from a resolver test. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Hosting Models / No-Code and Stored Views

requirements.text: The producer MUST signal `producer` resolution in the stored view's capabilities. Storing files alone does not imply that federation has been performed. A stored Registry intended for consumer-side composition retains the default `consumer` behavior.

review.note: Stored capability readers preserve enabled owner and reject malformed data. Snapshot writers' producer signaling must be assessed with the selected publication workflow, not inferred from merely storing a capability object. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Hosting Models / No-Code and Stored Views

requirements.text: Core single-document exports and multiple-document views remain available. The [directory mapping](../bindings/mapping.md) and [OCI](../bindings/oci.md) bindings additionally define storage formats with explicit content and integrity references. Their [snapshot completeness](#snapshots-and-completeness) rules identify which content has been captured. A live resolver MAY consume these stored snapshots as source Registries.

review.note: Directory mapping and OCI are separate snapshot formats; HTTP exports and full cross-binding producer materialization remain their owning gates. Native selective reads are not a full export proof. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Hosting Models / Signaling Who Performs Resolution

requirements.text: The OPTIONAL `federation` extension in the Registry's enabled [Core capabilities](../../core/spec.md#registry-capabilities) identifies who performs federation resolution for the selected view. It is not a catalog attribute, an `xref` value, or an entry in the `flags` array.

review.note: Ownership is parsed only from the enabled capabilities federation object, not flags or catalog data. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Hosting Models / Signaling Who Performs Resolution

requirements.text: The extension is an object containing the REQUIRED string field `resolution`. Its values are case-sensitive:

review.note: Owner values are required strings and case-sensitive; malformed and unknown values retain distinct errors. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Hosting Models / Signaling Who Performs Resolution

requirements.text: If the `federation` capability is absent, the consumer MUST use `consumer`. This preserves the default behavior for existing Registries. If the capability is present, `resolution` MUST be present and MUST be a string. Malformed data produces `invalid_package`. An unknown owner value or unsupported field produces `unsupported_operation`. It MUST NOT silently fall back to consumer-side resolution.

review.note: Absence defaults to consumer; malformed extension is invalid, unknown owner/fields are unsupported, never fallback. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Hosting Models / Signaling Who Performs Resolution

requirements.text: A federation-aware consumer MUST inspect this signal before traversing a view's catalog. It obtains enabled capabilities through the selected binding's capability read or an equivalent inlined representation. An offered capability is not the enabled value. A failed metadata read is not an absent signal and MUST be handled according to that binding's error rules.

review.note: The HTTP source establishes enabled capabilities before model-dependent reads and retains missing-API evidence separately. Resolver owner inspection precedes source traversal. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Hosting Models / Signaling Who Performs Resolution

requirements.text: With `producer`, the consumer MUST NOT use the view's catalog to repeat composition for the same request. This applies to entity reads, collection enumeration, label selection and default/explicit Version reads. A `not_found` or other failure returned by the producer MUST NOT trigger fallback through that producer's catalog. A producer therefore advertises this value only when it handles resolution for the whole view it exposes, not a partially combined result requiring its consumer to finish the work.

review.note: Producer ownership short-circuits source composition and sends the original request directly. Neither a miss nor a failed producer response probes downstream sources. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Hosting Models / Signaling Who Performs Resolution

requirements.text: The value applies to the selected Registry root, access context and revision. A capture MUST retain the value appropriate to its resulting view, not copy `producer` from an upstream view whose composition it has not preserved. Consumers MUST keep that choice for the operation. Observing it change during a consistent multi-read capture produces `inconsistent_snapshot`.

review.note: Every consumed source context and enabled owner stays fixed across the whole operation, including gaps between probes and Version reads and earlier collection captures. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Resolving a Consumer Request / Local Resources and Ordered Sources

requirements.text: The federating Registry MUST use an explicit composition policy identifying the eligible catalog entries, their order and the Resource paths they can supply. That ordered list is configuration, not JSON object-map order or Category enumeration order. This specification does not add a catalog attribute for that list. A caller MAY choose one source explicitly instead. An unordered set of potentially competing origins is insufficient to choose a winner and MUST produce `ambiguous` when disambiguation is needed.

review.note: Composition receives an explicit source order and compatibility predicate. Unordered competitors are ambiguous; JSON ordering is not an implicit policy. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Resolving a Consumer Request / Local Resources and Ordered Sources

requirements.text: 1. Check the requested Resource path in the local Registry view. A present local Resource wins, including a local alias. Its missing Version or unavailable document MUST NOT be filled from another Registry.

review.note: Local Resource presence fixes the origin for the whole Resource and cannot be filled by another source's Version. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Resolving a Consumer Request / Local Resources and Ordered Sources

requirements.text: 3. Resolve the same typed Resource XID in the selected source context. A policy that projects a different source path MUST define that mapping explicitly. The source's model and data MUST be compatible with the consumer-visible model for that path.

review.note: Nonlocal results require the explicit caller's consumer-model/projection check before acceptance. Wrong typed collection/member identities fail instead of being relabeled. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Resolving a Consumer Request / Local Resources and Ordered Sources

requirements.text: 5. Stop at the first found Resource. Select its requested Version, or its Core default Version, and obtain the requested representation. All Meta, Version and document reads for this Resource MUST use that selected origin and revision. Do not merge Version sets across origins.

review.note: First eligible Resource selection retains one source for Meta, Version and content reads, with no cross-origin Version merge. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Resolving a Consumer Request / Local Resources and Ordered Sources

requirements.text: 6. A source Resource result of `not_found` permits trying the next configured source entry. Exhausting the list yields `not_found`. Other failures, including authorization denial, unsupported binding/version, malformed data and integrity failure, MUST be reported rather than treated as absence.

review.note: Only a Resource NotFound permits the next source. Denial and malformed/unsupported source responses retain failures and stop selection. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Resolving a Consumer Request / Collections and Selection

requirements.text: A federating server exposing a combined Group or Resource collection MUST enumerate all eligible source collections needed for that view and apply the same Resource-level precedence before returning members. A shadowed source Resource contributes no additional Versions or alternate label values. Configured source type mappings MUST account for the collection's model.

review.note: The Resource resolver consumes complete source collections and applies Resource-level precedence. All Group projection/type mapping remains with the producer frontend gate. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Resolving a Consumer Request / Collections and Selection

requirements.text: A label selector is then evaluated on the resulting visible collection. Finding one matching member in an early source is not proof of uniqueness. All necessary collection pages and unshadowed sources MUST be considered. Errors or incomplete traversal MUST NOT be disguised as a complete result. Counts, continuation links and model/capability reads MUST describe the consumer-visible Registry, not whichever source happened to respond first.

review.note: Complete-source label uniqueness is directly enforced; producer-facing counts, cursors and model/capability composition need their separate full frontend evidence. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Discovery and Binding Selection

requirements.text: A resolver MUST select a catalog-description Version before interpreting its advertisements. In the absence of an explicit description Version, it MUST use the catalog Resource's Core default Version. A resolver MUST NOT infer an API from `weburl`, a label, a category name or a descriptive relationship. A website-only entry is a valid catalog entry, but is not resolvable.

review.note: CatalogDescription.FromResource selects Meta-default or an explicit exact Version before advertisements. Websites and descriptive links cannot become candidates. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Discovery and Binding Selection

requirements.text: The domain's `federationprofiles` array contains advertisements with `name`, `endpoint`, OPTIONAL `priority` and OPTIONAL `parameters`. Profile names are case-sensitive. The names defined by this family are:

review.note: Advertisement shape, ordinal profile names, optional priority and parameter objects are checked before selection. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Discovery and Binding Selection

requirements.text: | `opcua` | Native UA endpoint URL | `registryroot`: portable NodeId. OPTIONAL `applicationuri` and `transportprofileuri`. |

review.note: The OPC-UA-specific binding is excluded by the approved scope. Its advertisement can remain opaque catalog data, but this implementation does not claim that native binding. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Discovery and Binding Selection

requirements.text: The bindings define parameter grammars and their supported transports. Endpoints MUST be absolute URIs and MUST NOT embed credentials. A selected built-in advertisement with an unknown parameter MUST produce `unsupported_operation`. Silently ignoring a parameter could select a different Registry or revision. An unknown profile name remains valid catalog metadata, but MUST NOT be executed as a known profile.

review.note: Shared common validation checks absolute credential-free locators. Selected unknown built-in parameters remain unsupported, never stripped; unknown names execute only if the caller explicitly registers that profile. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Discovery and Binding Selection

requirements.text: An absent `priority` means zero. Lower unsigned integer values are preferred. An absent `parameters` means an empty object. Selection MUST proceed as follows:

review.note: Selection applies explicit caller choice/policy, supported profiles, unsigned arbitrary-precision priority and stable original order. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Discovery and Binding Selection

requirements.text: A present `xregurl` contributes an implicit HTTP advertisement of priority zero, after explicit advertisements for tie-breaking. This applies even if an explicit advertisement names the same endpoint at another priority. If explicit HTTP advertisements exist, at least one endpoint MUST equal `xregurl` exactly. This exact comparison is a consistency rule, not a definition of URI identity.

review.note: Implicit HTTP is appended at zero priority; explicit-HTTP/xregurl consistency uses exact source text, before exclusion. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Discovery and Binding Selection

requirements.text: No candidate yields `unsupported_binding`. A caller rejection yields `policy_denied`. An attempted binding MUST NOT silently fail over after an integrity error, version mismatch, policy rejection, ambiguous selection or inconsistent snapshot. A caller MAY initiate another operation with an explicitly different advertisement after inspecting the failure. A producer's multiple endpoints claim the same logical Registry, not necessarily the same instantaneous state. Credentials and trust are established independently.

review.note: No supported candidate and explicit policy denial remain distinct. CatalogSourceSelection invokes one factory and propagates the selected acquisition failure without trying another advertisement. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Read Operations

requirements.text: A Resource document request selects its Core default Version. An explicit Version request selects exactly that Version, case-sensitively. Neither operation selects the greatest Version string, latest OCI tag, newest Git commit or most recently modified file. Metadata-only Resources have no domain document. Requesting one MUST produce `unsupported_operation`.

review.note: Resource Document reads use Meta.defaultversionid and explicit Version reads preserve exact identity; no-document Resource types fail before fetching bytes. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Read Operations

requirements.text: For each operation a resolver MUST:

review.note: Bindings establish typed models, capabilities, base locators and revision semantics. Full aggregate evidence for every listed context-establishment substep across all bindings remains with binding qualification. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Read Operations

requirements.text: Origin information MUST identify the chosen advertisement, catalog-description Version when applicable, target XID and revision pin or the absence of an immutable pin. It MUST travel separately from Core identity attributes. A standalone endpoint supplied by the caller MAY bypass catalog discovery, but MUST still establish all other context.

review.note: Catalog-directed acquisition now retains exact chosen advertisement and description Version XID with the catalog context, separate from target Registry revision and selected content XID. Standalone contexts remain valid without a catalog origin. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Read Operations

requirements.text: If a model is captured, the package MUST preserve enough model source to retain Resource type sharing. An expanded model alone can obscure `ximportresources` provenance. Included model documents MUST be resolved within the captured scope, or supplied with immutable checked references. Offline-complete interpretation MUST NOT fetch mutable external includes. Unknown Core versions MUST NOT be accepted merely because a document parses.

review.note: Captured source and effective model remain distinct, known authored/include precedence is checked, and offline readers do not acquire external includes. Unknown Core versions fail before model interpretation. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Identity and References

requirements.text: An XID identifies an entity only within one Registry. Resolvers MUST preserve both its Registry context and typed collection path. Equal XIDs in unrelated Registries are not evidence that the entities or their bytes are identical. Core IDs are unique case-insensitively within their parent, but are looked up case-sensitively. Storage bindings MUST NOT weaken either rule.

review.note: Context and typed path are both retained. IDs are decoded once, looked up ordinally and checked for case-insensitive collisions within a collection. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Identity and References / Local Cross-References

requirements.text: Core [`meta.xref`](../../core/spec.md#cross-referencing-resources) remains an intra-Registry Resource XID. Federation chooses a source Registry through the catalog and composition policy, rather than adding a remote meaning to this Core attribute. Its source and target MUST have the same Resource model type. Structurally identical independent definitions are insufficient. Sharing between Group types uses [`ximportresources`](../../core/model.md#reuse-of-resource-definitions).

review.note: Core one-hop aliases use same-Registry XIDs and actual shared imported Resource model identity, not structural similarity. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Identity and References / Local Cross-References

requirements.text: An alias in `/mirrors/local/assets/copy` can then carry `meta.xref: "/documents/main/assets/item"`. When Core calls for inherited target metadata, source IDs and navigation MUST remain source-relative. If the target is itself an alias, a resolver MUST NOT follow another `xref`. If the target is unavailable, Core's minimal ID-like alias serialization applies. This is not automatically `not_found` for the source.

review.note: Source alias identity remains source-relative; target aliases are not traversed again and dangling target instances preserve the source's minimal identity behavior. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Identity and References / Local Cross-References

requirements.text: A malformed XID or nonexistent model type is not the same as a dangling entity instance. Core's malformed-reference rules still apply. Document view MUST NOT expand the target. A document-view request for an alias's Versions or an individual Version MUST retain Core's `cannot_doc_xref` behavior. This specification does not add remote writes to aliases.

review.note: Malformed references and unsupported alias-Version Doc views remain distinct from dangling instances; Doc views never expand alias targets. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Identity and References / Remote References and Composition

requirements.text: A Version's `<RESOURCE>url` references a domain document. It MUST NOT be interpreted as remote Resource metadata or as a request to import Versions. Reading its bytes does not change the identity of the describing Version.

review.note: External domain locators remain unfetched descriptors tied to the selected Version, not metadata imports or successful empty content. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Identity and References / Remote References and Composition

requirements.text: A projected Registry MAY expose locally modeled Resources representing external content. Any `xref` it exposes MUST satisfy Core within that projected Registry. A projection MUST NOT equate resources solely because their XIDs collide. Competing origins require an explicit selection or `ambiguous`, not an undocumented winner. A shared logical-identity policy can be defined by a domain, but does not alter XID scope.

review.note: Consumer composition detects competing origins and refuses URI-identity collisions. Complete producer alias-origin and domain projection policy remains with the frontend gate. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Identity and References / Reference Bases

requirements.text: A resolver MUST NOT substitute one of these bases for another. A binding that cannot preserve or supply the base needed to interpret a relative document URI MUST report `invalid_package` or `unsupported_operation` rather than guess.

review.note: Document base/origin, Core navigation and storage root remain separate. Packaging never fetches or reinterprets relative external descriptors under an invented base. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Selectors

requirements.text: The `label` names a map key. `value` is a literal string. Labels MAY be absent, and an empty string value is valid. An absent key does not match an empty value. Comparison MUST follow Core's case-insensitive string filtering. En-US Unicode collation is STRONGLY RECOMMENDED by Core. This specification adds neither mandatory language keys nor NFC normalization. Map-key selection remains exact. Comparison applies to the selected value.

review.note: Label keys remain exact; values compare as literal case-insensitive strings. Missing versus empty and normalization/wildcard-looking strings are distinct. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Selectors

requirements.text: A resolver using a transport filter MUST escape its literal value and attribute path under that binding. `*`, `\`, `.` or an operator in a selector MUST NOT accidentally become a wildcard or another expression. Implementations MAY instead enumerate and compare locally. An optimization MUST NOT change the matching or ambiguity outcome.

review.note: Selection enumerates unfiltered and compares locally; no transport-filter interpolation can promote literal syntax to operators. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Selectors

requirements.text: Zero matches yields `not_found`. Exactly one complete match yields the selected entity. Multiple matches yields `ambiguous`. A resolver MUST inspect all necessary continuation pages before claiming uniqueness. It MAY report ambiguity after a second match without reading further pages. A request limit, incomplete page chain or unstable collection MUST NOT be reported as a unique selection. Resource selectors examine the effective metadata of their default Versions as defined by Core, not only the reduced Resource object in document view.

review.note: Uniqueness follows complete pages and visible origins. Doc Resource labels come from actual default-Version metadata, with metadata-only fallback and default consistency checks. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Representations

requirements.text: Metadata and domain documents are distinct results, even when both are JSON. `self`, `metaurl` and `defaultversionurl` locate metadata under the relevant Core binding. They MUST NOT automatically be treated as raw-byte locations.

review.note: Metadata navigation is not raw content; typed Document operations and metadata envelopes preserve that distinction even for JSON and metadata-only models. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Representations

requirements.text: Native access to a [snapshot](#snapshots-and-completeness) uses Core [document view](../../core/spec.md#doc-flag), with storage descriptors and transport context outside the Core entity. This requires removal of duplicated default-Version attributes, Version validation-result attributes and `shortself`, and suppression of alias-target expansion. Links to entities included in the returned document MUST use document-local JSON Pointers. Links to entities not included MUST NOT be rewritten to nonexistent local pointers. Reassembling records into a larger document requires rebasing pointers to that document, not concatenating independently relative records.

review.note: Mapping Doc navigation/alias/default shaping has direct evidence. All native bindings and transformed producer validation-flag suppression remain with their current completion gates. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Representations

requirements.text: Native bindings MUST distinguish these document-view serializations from the logical operation that retrieves an alias's target document under Core. An unsupported view or alias-Version document view MUST be reported, not silently converted to a different view.

review.note: Alias Document bytes and alias-Version Doc metadata are different operations; unsupported views preserve cannot_doc_xref instead of being switched silently. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Representations

requirements.text: A binding offering API-view results MUST define actually retrievable Core-conforming `self` and navigation URLs. An implementation-defined URI with no retrieval contract is insufficient. An OPTIONAL HTTP facade MUST conform separately to [Core HTTP](../../core/http.md). Neither `oci://` locators nor UA NodeIds become Core XIDs.

review.note: Native mapping rejects unsupported API view rather than inventing retrieval URLs; HTTP source navigation is real. The optional producer HTTP facade has a separate protocol gate. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Representations

requirements.text: Formats MUST preserve extension attributes and domain bytes. A zero-byte document is present content and MUST NOT be replaced by `{}`, `null` or a missing document. Binary documents MUST NOT pass through text conversion.

review.note: Documents retain byte identity and empty presence; extension metadata is not altered by catalog-origin annotation or document wrapping. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Snapshots and Completeness

requirements.text: Every snapshot MUST have a complete internal containment graph. A linked snapshot MAY retain explicit external document references. An offline-complete snapshot MUST additionally contain the declared xRegistry document content for its selected scope and the model material needed to interpret it. The producer MUST identify that scope and completeness class. Missing internally referenced data is an invalid package in either class.

review.note: Mapping's exhaustive validation distinguishes complete internal graph and offline external-content requirements. Full snapshot producer and OCI publication completion is owned by the binding gates. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Snapshots and Completeness

requirements.text: Offline completeness does not mean copying all cataloged Registries or discovering arbitrary links inside every domain document. External reference bases and known content integrity descriptors MUST survive packaging. Materializing external content requires preserving its actual bytes.

review.note: Full linked validation does not crawl catalog/domain URLs or unreferenced files; descriptors retain explicit bases and exact content bytes. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Snapshots and Completeness

requirements.text: An immutable revision MUST remain pinned throughout an operation. A moving tag, branch or mutable directory name is not a revision pin. A live HTTP or UA endpoint without a snapshot guarantee MUST be reported as live, not as an atomic snapshot. Revision identifiers MUST NOT be substituted for Resource Version IDs.

review.note: Native context and the HTTP adapter distinguish pins from live observations, and composition fixes the context throughout an operation. All immutable Git/OCI acquisition cells remain binding-specific evidence, not inferred here. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Snapshots and Completeness

requirements.text: Digests identify exact bytes, not semantic equality. Equivalent publications can have different digests. New snapshots MAY reuse unchanged content and subtrees, but MUST be readable without replaying older snapshots.

review.note: Mapping verifies exact digest before parsing. Independent readability of reused OCI publication subtrees is a separate producer obligation still under the OCI completion gate. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Errors

requirements.text: An error MUST retain the underlying Core error or transport diagnostic when available, without exposing credentials. An incomplete retrieval MUST NOT be returned as a successful empty collection. Core's dangling-alias exception is preserved.

review.note: Failures retain Core/HTTP diagnostics without becoming empty collections; detached HTTP problem data is explicitly untrusted rather than safe public logging. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Security Considerations

requirements.text: Catalog data and package contents are untrusted input. Discovery is not an authorization grant. A resolver MUST apply caller policy before contacting endpoints, following redirects, reading local paths or retrieving external documents. Credentials MUST be scoped to the authenticated destination and MUST NOT be forwarded merely because a catalog entry or redirect names it.

review.note: Catalog selection and source factories keep authorization separate and deny before dispatch. The full outbound DNS/socket/redirect/File policy matrix is a separate security/binding gate, not proved by catalog syntax. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Security Considerations

requirements.text: Resolvers MUST bound traversal depth, request count and aggregate bytes, detect discovery/redirect cycles, and surface exhausted bounds. SHA-256 integrity does not authenticate a publisher. Signature and provenance policies are separate from containment completeness. Git readers MUST NOT execute repository content. Filesystem readers MUST enforce containment including symlinks and reparse points.

review.note: Generic budgets, source and catalog-hop limits, cancellation and HTTP shared accounting are directly exercised. Git no-execution and filesystem containment/provenance remain separate binding/security obligations. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Conformance

requirements.text: A **federation resolver** MUST implement resolution-owner signaling, selection, context, Core semantics, representations and failures above and identify each implemented binding. Conformance to one binding does not imply support for another.

review.note: This is an aggregate conformance claim over all preceding resolver and binding obligations; individual public-seam evidence does not qualify every native platform or binding. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Conformance

requirements.text: A **snapshot producer** MUST identify its format, scope and linked or offline-complete class and produce a complete internal graph. An OPTIONAL API facade requires separate protocol-binding conformance.

review.note: This is an aggregate snapshot-producer/facade conformance claim and requires its owning publication and protocol gates. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Conformance

requirements.text: The executable examples are offline conformance aids, not production resolvers. [Shared vectors](samples/selection.json) distinguish identity, selection and reference cases. Binding fixtures exercise transport-specific retrieval. Tests MUST distinguish full graph validation from selective lookup. A validator walking everything does not demonstrate efficient selective resolution.

review.note: Selective lookup and exhaustive closure validation have independent tests. A selected valid object cannot certify unvisited corrupt or missing content. Reviewed against the complete source context and public regression behavior. This is implementation evidence, not release qualification or an unexecuted native-platform claim.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Notations and Scope

requirements.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" are to be interpreted as described in [RFC2119][rfc2119].

review.note: RFC2119 terminology is not a separate executable obligation. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Notations and Scope

requirements.text: Core owns entity types, IDs, labels, default Versions, `xref`, document view, errors and request flags. The HTTP binding owns methods, paths, `$details`, HTTP metadata headers and the wire representation of flags. [HTTP Semantics][http] and [HTTP Caching][cache] own HTTP processing. Requirements here apply to federation resolvers. They do not turn an OPTIONAL Core API into a mandatory server API or redefine CRUD operations.

review.note: The scope preserves Core/HTTP ownership and optional server APIs; this is an interpretation boundary. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Advertisement and Bootstrap

requirements.text: An HTTP advertisement has `name: "http"`, an absolute HTTP(S) Registry-root `endpoint`, and no parameters in this version. Its endpoint MUST NOT have embedded credentials, a query or a fragment. Unknown parameters on the selected advertisement MUST produce `unsupported_operation`.

review.note: Shared Catalog validation enforces absolute credential-free HTTP roots and selected-parameter rejection without acquisition. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Advertisement and Bootstrap

requirements.text: Selection, priorities, ties and implicit `xregurl` handling follow [Federation discovery](../federation/spec.md#discovery-and-binding-selection). If explicit HTTP advertisements coexist with `xregurl`, one endpoint MUST match `xregurl` exactly. `weburl` is a website, not an API fallback.

review.note: Exact explicit-HTTP/xregurl agreement is distinct from URI normalization and website metadata is not a fallback. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Advertisement and Bootstrap

requirements.text: A resolver bootstrapping from a catalog MUST read the catalog model before interpreting its `categories` / `registries` collections. These catalog Resources have `hasdocument: false`. Their Version metadata contains `xregurl`, `weburl` and any `federationprofiles`. It is not a domain document to download. An explicit catalog-description Version selects that Version. Otherwise, the catalog Resource's Core default Version applies. The described Registry's `registryid` need not equal the catalog entry ID.

review.note: The source establishes its model before typed reads and CatalogDescription selects Meta-default/explicit Versions. A standalone endpoint bypasses discovery; a general catalog-driven acquisition workflow is not claimed by these source-level APIs. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Advertisement and Bootstrap

requirements.text: The chosen advertisement establishes a new Registry context. The resolver MUST discover the target's version, model and capabilities independently of the catalog. It MUST NOT transfer catalog credentials, compatibility assumptions or label requirements to that target.

review.note: Each explicitly opened HTTP source owns a separate isolated client and independently verifies its version/model/capabilities; advertisements do not carry incoming credentials into that client. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Registry Root and Version Discovery

requirements.text: The advertised root can have an arbitrary base path. For example, XID `/documents/main/assets/item` at `https://first.example.com/services/xreg/` is below `/services/xreg/documents/main/assets/item`, not `/documents/main/assets/item`. The root request uses the advertised root itself. Descendant construction MUST retain its complete base path, preserve case-sensitive Core IDs and encode URI path segments without double encoding. A resolver MUST NOT derive global entity identity by splitting an arbitrary URL.

review.note: The selected root's full base path and exact decoded Core IDs are preserved, with one escape pass when constructing descendant requests. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Registry Root and Version Discovery

requirements.text: The HTTP binding's `Link` with `rel=xregistry-root` identifies the serving Registry root when provided. A resolver MUST interpret it in the response context and apply the same locator policy as for other links. A relocated root does not silently authorize access to a different origin.

review.note: Observe checks serving-root links against origin/root and rejects relocation without explicit source selection. The complete relative/anchor/relocation matrix is not directly mapped by this review. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Registry Root and Version Discovery

requirements.text: The resolver MUST obtain `specversion` from the Registry representation before interpreting model-dependent entities. A known, explicitly supported Core version is necessary. Parsing JSON is not a compatibility check. An unsupported version MUST produce `unsupported_version`. If supported, Core's `specversion` flag can request a compatible representation, but the resolver MUST verify the version actually returned. Silently ignoring a query parameter MUST NOT be mistaken for successful negotiation.

review.note: Bootstrap reads specversion before model-dependent data and rejects incompatible versions. It does not infer negotiation success from ignored query flags. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Registry Root and Version Discovery

requirements.text: `GET B/capabilities` retrieves enabled capabilities. A resolver MAY use already inlined capabilities or request supported inlining. It MUST NOT assume that `filter`, `inline`, pagination, `/export` or writes are enabled. Before composing the selected view, it MUST apply the shared [resolution-owner signal](../federation/spec.md#signaling-who-performs-resolution). `federation.resolution: "producer"` means read the view directly without traversing its catalog. An absent signal defaults to consumer resolution. An absent capabilities API, an absent flag, or `flags: null` provides no positive evidence for that flag. `/capabilitiesoffered` describes choices that can be enabled, not what is currently enabled.

review.note: Enabled capability evidence remains distinct from offered/absent data; flags use Core case-insensitive names and no unsupported view is assumed. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Registry Root and Version Discovery

requirements.text: When an OPTIONAL read API is unavailable, a resolver MAY use an equivalent already obtained representation, a supported inline request, or an advertised Core `/export` document. It MUST preserve the requested view and completeness. If no equivalent read exists, it MUST return `unsupported_operation`, not an invented empty entity or collection.

review.note: Already inlined root material is reused; unavailable capabilities have no fabricated representation. Valid unresolved includes fail UnsupportedOperation unless a bounded explicitly authorized resolver is supplied. Optional additional equivalent-export fallback is not claimed. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Native Read Mapping

requirements.text: The existing `GET B/export` convenience path, if supported, is precisely `GET B?doc&inline=*,capabilities,modelsource` with Core's flag semantics. It is not a federation-specific snapshot API. A resolver consuming an export MUST resolve document-local pointers within that returned document.

review.note: The consumer source does not claim an export acquisition workflow. Producer export support is a distinct optional frontend concern and remains explicit. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Metadata, Documents and Versions

requirements.text: Resource metadata, the Meta entity and Version metadata are separate views. In particular, a Resource's API-view `versionid` is the default Version projection, whereas `meta.defaultversionid` records the choice. A resolver MUST NOT choose a default by lexical order, modification time, enumeration order or the greatest Version identifier.

review.note: Default selection comes from Resource Meta, never lexical/time order or a transport revision. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Metadata, Documents and Versions

requirements.text: An explicit Version target MUST select that exact, case-sensitive Version. When a multi-request operation needs both default metadata and bytes, the resolver SHOULD record the selected default Version ID and use its explicit Version URLs for subsequent requests. It MUST detect a changed selection when claiming a consistent capture. Version IDs themselves do not make a live Version immutable.

review.note: Default capture records an explicit Version, rechecks its selection, and classifies failed dependent reads as inconsistent while preserving direct-Version error semantics. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Metadata, Documents and Versions

requirements.text: For document-bearing types, body `self` links to Resource/Version metadata include `$details` in API view, as specified by Core HTTP. Metadata-only types' `self` links MUST NOT include it. In document view, pointers are relative to the returned JSON and never include `$details`. The resolver MUST preserve Core navigation semantics rather than replace `self` with an endpoint label.

review.note: The model selects $details only for document-bearing metadata; Doc pointers are rebased only at known navigation paths and retain collection member prefixes. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Metadata, Documents and Versions

requirements.text: Raw document reads use the domain media type and bytes. Core's `xRegistry-` headers carry accompanying metadata. `Content-Location`, when present on a default read, identifies the default Version as Core specifies. A zero-byte document is a successful empty byte sequence, not a missing document. Absent content and metadata-only types MUST remain distinguishable. For byte-preserving capture, raw Version reads or supported Core `binary` serialization are appropriate. Reparsing and pretty-printing JSON is not byte preservation.

review.note: Document bytes remain exact and zero bytes remain present. Accompanying Version header values are decoded once and compared to the selected identity; malformed headers do not become raw exceptions. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Metadata, Documents and Versions

requirements.text: Core `meta.xref` remains same-Registry, same Resource model type and one hop. Source IDs and navigation remain source-relative. A dangling target or a target that is itself an alias keeps Core's minimal source serialization. Document view MUST NOT expand an alias. Document-view requests below its `versions` preserve `cannot_doc_xref`. Federation MUST NOT reinterpret an absolute remote URL as `xref`.

review.note: Source-local aliases use actual compiled Resource type identity and at most one hop; requested Doc views remain unexpanded and cannot masquerade as API data. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Literal Label Selection

requirements.text: The common selector is an exact label-key lookup and a Core case-insensitive comparison of string values. Labels are OPTIONAL. Values can be empty. An absent label does not match an empty value. The resolver MUST NOT require a language label, impose NFC normalization, infer a locale from a category, or interpret the caller's `*` as a wildcard.

review.note: Labels are exact keys with literal case-insensitive values, including empty values; no category/locale/NFC/wildcard inference. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Literal Label Selection

requirements.text: A supported HTTP filter is an optimization. The resolver MUST construct Core dot notation relative to the requested collection and preserve literal meaning. It MUST escape a literal wildcard using Core's backslash escape before URI encoding. It MUST quote label keys containing dot-notation operators using Core bracket notation. For example:

review.note: Transport filtering is not used by this source. The permitted unfiltered local-selection path avoids inventing unsupported escaping extensions. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Literal Label Selection

requirements.text: The common selector is narrower than Core's filter language. For example, the literal string `null` is not Core's missing-attribute expression. If literal commas, quotes, backslashes or other syntax cannot be represented unambiguously by a supported filter, the resolver MUST use local selection over an unfiltered collection rather than invent an escaping extension. URI encoding alone does not escape Core expression syntax.

review.note: All selection stays local and unfiltered, preserving wildcard-looking or otherwise ambiguous Core filter text literally. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Literal Label Selection

requirements.text: The resolver MUST apply the same literal comparison to returned candidates even when filtering was requested. Core permits unsupported query flags to be ignored. A nonempty response therefore does not prove that the filter was implemented.

review.note: Returned candidates are locally compared instead of trusting an ignored filter flag or nonempty response. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Pagination and No-Filter Fallback

requirements.text: A resolver MUST process collection pages according to the [pagination specification](../../pagination/spec.md). It MUST follow each necessary `Link` with `rel=next`, resolve a relative link against the response request URL, and then use that link without editing its query. It MUST NOT synthesize page numbers, reattach the original filter, or add `limit` to subsequent links. Pagination links have the same credential and locator policy checks as redirects.

review.note: Every needed opaque next link is followed without reattaching initial query flags, within the same credential/root policy and request budget. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Pagination and No-Filter Fallback

requirements.text: Unique label selection requires the complete relevant candidate set. A match on the first page is not proof of uniqueness. No match after complete enumeration yields `not_found`. A second match yields `ambiguous`. An unavailable later page or a traversal limit MUST NOT become either a unique result or `not_found`. Conflicting duplicates, changed declared totals or an incomplete capture MUST be reported, not silently merged.

review.note: Later-page failures, duplicate identities, changed counts and repeated links cannot become complete unique results; case-only IDs are rejected. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Pagination and No-Filter Fallback

requirements.text: If filtering is unavailable, the resolver MUST enumerate the relevant unfiltered collection and apply the common selector locally. This applies to no-code endpoints as well as API servers. It SHOULD use metadata already present in collection responses and avoid unrelated document downloads. Neither filtering nor inlining is a prerequisite for HTTP federation.

review.note: Local comparison uses existing default-Version metadata where present, otherwise only metadata acquisition, never unrelated domain bytes. Fallback checks any already captured default. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Pagination and No-Filter Fallback

requirements.text: An endpoint that advertises `pagination: false` normally supplies its complete collection in one response. If a next link is nevertheless returned, the resolver MUST NOT claim completeness until it has handled that link or reported the conflicting behavior. A collection `count` alone is not a replacement for the members or next links.

review.note: A contradictory pagination:false advertisement does not suppress necessary next-link handling. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / HTTP Validators and Partial Content

requirements.text: ETags are opaque, representation-scoped validators, not XIDs, Core epochs, global content digests or Registry-wide revision pins. Metadata and document URLs, query variants and content codings can have different validators. The resolver MUST use the selected representation's validator with that representation, respecting `Vary`, cache directives and authorization scope.

review.note: Observations retain representation URI, ETag, Vary, coding and cache/authorization context. Shared cache or conditional validator use is not enabled; full cache conformance is therefore not claimed. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / HTTP Validators and Partial Content

requirements.text: Conditional `GET` with `If-None-Match` uses HTTP's weak comparison and can revalidate a cached response. `304 Not Modified` has no replacement body. The resolver MUST use an applicable stored response and update it according to RFC 9111 section 4.3.4. Without one, it needs an unconditional read or an explicit failure. `If-Modified-Since` and `Last-Modified` have HTTP's semantics and precedence, not Core timestamp semantics.

review.note: This no-cache source never treats an unsolicited 304 as a replacement body; it fails explicitly without an applicable cached response. No RFC9111 update algorithm is claimed. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / HTTP Validators and Partial Content

requirements.text: `If-Match` uses strong comparison. A weak ETag MUST NOT be used where a strong validator is needed. A resolver assembling partial bytes MUST apply RFC 9110 sections 13.1.5 and 14, validate `Content-Range` and representation identity, and account for every byte. A weak ETag is not valid for `If-Range`. An HTTP-date is usable there only under HTTP's strong-validator conditions. If an `If-Range` request returns a complete `200` response, the resolver MUST replace, not append to, its partial bytes.

review.note: The source does not send If-Range/If-Match or join partial bytes. Unrequested partial data is rejected instead of claiming a complete representation. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / HTTP Validators and Partial Content

requirements.text: A `206` response is not a complete document merely because the transfer ended successfully. Missing ranges, truncation, changed validators or unverified joins MUST NOT produce a complete snapshot. A failed conditional read used to hold a capture stable, including `412`, yields `inconsistent_snapshot`.

review.note: 206/412 and interrupted dependent captures are inconsistent, never complete snapshots. Error details/status are retained. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / HTTP Validators and Partial Content

requirements.text: A gateway that transforms a representation MUST NOT blindly forward the upstream strong ETag as the validator for different bytes. It has to preserve HTTP validator semantics for its own representation or omit that validator. Federation imposes no unchanged-upstream-ETag requirement.

review.note: The producer frontend omits upstream validators for transformed output and uses no-store. Complete transformed response/header evidence remains owned by the broader Bridge review. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Redirects and Authorization Boundaries

requirements.text: Redirect processing follows RFC 9110 section 15.4 and Core HTTP. In particular, a Core external document can yield `303 See Other` with an empty body and `Location` matching `<RESOURCE>url`. The destination is domain content, not another Registry root. Other redirects can relocate an endpoint or representation. The resolver MUST distinguish these cases.

review.note: 303 is accepted only as an empty external-Document descriptor agreeing with Version metadata, not another Registry context. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Redirects and Authorization Boundaries

requirements.text: Every redirect, advertised endpoint, next link and external document URL MUST pass caller policy, including scheme, destination, network access and redirect limits. The resolver MUST reject embedded credentials and MUST NOT automatically forward Authorization, cookies, client credentials or origin-specific conditional headers across a trust boundary. Destination credentials require independent authorization. HTTPS downgrade and access to restricted network locations require explicit policy, not an implicit fallback.

review.note: The isolated client/source enforces origin/credential/locator policy and returns external descriptors without fetching. A separately authorized redirect-acquisition/cache workflow is not implemented and is not disguised as success. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Redirects and Authorization Boundaries

requirements.text: `401` and `403` MUST NOT cause silent retries against another advertisement, a public mirror, or a weaker authentication mode. Redirect loops and bounded traversal exhaustion produce `limit_exceeded`. Trust rejection produces `policy_denied`.

review.note: 401/403 do not retry another source or weaken authentication. Composition reports policy denial rather than treating it as a Resource miss. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Live Capture and Errors

requirements.text: A capture MUST record its selected root, actual Core version, selected Version IDs, retrieval scope, available validators and absence of an immutable pin separately from Core IDs. It MUST distinguish a live, best-effort observation from a producer-guaranteed snapshot. A resolver requiring a stronger guarantee MUST fail explicitly when the endpoint cannot provide it. If the necessary capture operation is unsupported, the outcome is `unsupported_operation`. If an attempted capture is inconsistent or incomplete, the outcome is `inconsistent_snapshot`.

review.note: Source/Version/retrieval observations remain separate from Core identity and there is no immutable HTTP pin. Stronger snapshot requirements fail before acquisition. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Live Capture and Errors

requirements.text: For a multi-request capture, the resolver SHOULD recheck the default selection and the representations on which the capture depends. A changed default, changed representation, conflicting membership or interrupted page/byte sequence invalidates a claim of consistent capture. It MUST report `inconsistent_snapshot` and discard that claim. It MAY start a new, separately identified operation. A fresh capture is not a silent continuation using mixed old and new state.

review.note: Default and alias selections are rechecked, dependent interruption invalidates capture, and changed Doc/API default metadata is not mixed. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Federation / Live Capture and Errors

requirements.text: The resolver MUST retain the HTTP status and any Core error detail. `api_not_found` is not an absent entity. A generic `404` without enough context MUST NOT be used to invent an empty collection. Failure of a previously identified member during capture is also evidence of incomplete capture, not proof of a consistent deletion history.

review.note: Core/HTTP failures retain status and owned problem data. Generic404 cannot invent an empty collection, and a selected default's disappearance is not a successful deletion history. Direct source/public-regression evidence; no release or unexecuted-platform qualification.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Scope and Conventions

requirements.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119).

review.note: RFC2119 interpretation is not a separate runtime operation. Direct source/assertion review, not a release or all-platform qualification. Original sources and correction history are unchanged. source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Scope and Conventions

requirements.text: Both schemas use JSON Schema Draft 2020-12. Their URNs identify this draft's schemas. They are not network retrieval endpoints. Producers and consumers MUST also implement the semantic constraints below. Schema validity alone does not establish Core model compliance or graph completeness.

review.note: Captured metadata now uses Core model validation and explicit whole-closure validation. This compound producer/consumer statement still includes unimplemented external target validation and arbitrary domain semantic obligations; schema validity is not used as blanket conformance. Direct source/assertion review, not a release or all-platform qualification. Original sources and correction history are unchanged. SPEC-014 re-review: this exact clause and its neighboring scope are unchanged; only the metadata-only Document field-plane wording was corrected.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Root and Storage Paths

requirements.text: The selected directory MUST contain `registry.json`. Its record MUST have `kind: "registry"` and `entity.xid: "/"`. Git's `parameters.path` and File's endpoint select this same directory. Neither adds an implicit extra directory.

review.note: registry.json is opened exactly once and its kind/typed root identity checked. File and Git select their explicit roots; storage does not add an implicit directory. Direct source/assertion review, not a release or all-platform qualification. Original sources and correction history are unchanged. SPEC-014 re-review: this exact clause and its neighboring scope are unchanged; only the metadata-only Document field-plane wording was corrected.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Root and Storage Paths

requirements.text: Paths MUST be nonempty, normalized root-relative strings with `/` separators. They MUST NOT be absolute, contain empty components, `.` or `..` components, backslashes, NUL/control characters or surrogate code points. URI decoding MUST NOT be applied. Encoded separator/dot traversal tricks MUST be rejected. Portable paths MUST NOT contain `<>:"|?*`, end a component with a space or period, or use Windows device names such as `CON` and `NUL`. Other Unicode names and spaces within components are permitted. Platform path-length and access limits produce explicit errors.

review.note: StoragePath and the File reader reject traversal, aliases, unsafe names and links before reads. Full platform-specific length/access and every Unicode portability partition are not directly qualified by this row. Direct source/assertion review, not a release or all-platform qualification. Original sources and correction history are unchanged. SPEC-014 re-review: this exact clause and its neighboring scope are unchanged; only the metadata-only Document field-plane wording was corrected.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Root and Storage Paths

requirements.text: Metadata files describing different records or indexes MUST have distinct paths. Paths whose spellings differ only by case MUST NOT designate different mapping objects, because such mappings are ambiguous on case-insensitive filesystems. Several Versions MAY reference the same local document file using the same path and identical size/digest values. A document path MUST NOT also be allocated to a metadata record or index.

review.note: Register detects conflicting role, path-case, size, digest and entity allocation on visited objects; exhaustive validation walks all referenced objects. Complete cross-role/case/shared-Document negative partitions remain unproven. Direct source/assertion review, not a release or all-platform qualification. Original sources and correction history are unchanged. SPEC-014 re-review: this exact clause and its neighboring scope are unchanged; only the metadata-only Document field-plane wording was corrected.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Root and Storage Paths

requirements.text: Core's case-insensitive uniqueness within a parent and case-sensitive lookup still apply. A pair differing only in case in the same collection is invalid Core data, not a filesystem collision to repair. An ID MUST match the entire string against `[A-Za-z0-9_](?:[A-Za-z0-9_.~:@-]){0,127}`. Whitespace and trailing line terminators are not part of an ID. This grammar is independent of native filename rules. An implementation unable to represent the total path length or object count MUST report `limit_exceeded`. It MUST NOT truncate, normalize or replace an entity ID.

review.note: Decoded identifiers are validated once, selected case-sensitively and never converted to filesystem names. URI-equivalent and case-insensitive sibling collisions are rejected and operation limits are explicit. Direct source/assertion review, not a release or all-platform qualification. Original sources and correction history are unchanged. SPEC-014 re-review: this exact clause and its neighboring scope are unchanged; only the metadata-only Document field-plane wording was corrected.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Record and Index Documents

requirements.text: All record and index documents MUST be UTF-8 JSON objects without a byte order mark, duplicate keys or non-JSON numbers. Each has `format: "xregistry-document-tree"` and `formatversion: "1"`. An unknown version MUST produce `unsupported_version`.

review.note: Strict RegistryJson parsing and format/version checks are present. This review lacks an end-to-end mapping matrix for every malformed encoding, duplicate-number and unsupported-version case; shared parser tests alone do not close the row. Direct source/assertion review, not a release or all-platform qualification. Original sources and correction history are unchanged. SPEC-014 re-review: this exact clause and its neighboring scope are unchanged; only the metadata-only Document field-plane wording was corrected.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Record and Index Documents

requirements.text: | Kind | REQUIRED metadata in `entity`, in addition to `xid` |

It MUST NOT substitute the OCI repository or config path. Both OPTIONAL fields MUST be credential-free absolute URIs and MUST appear only in `embedded` mode. The selected snapshot supplies the pinned bytes, not a fresh fetch of the original locator.

requirements.text: Use authenticated HTTPS and repository-scoped credentials under caller policy. OCI metadata MUST NOT contain credentials. source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Notations and Terminology / Terminology / Resource

requirements.text: Resources, typically, represent the main data of interest for the Registry. In the filesystem analogy, these would be the "files". Each Resource MUST exist under a single Group and, similar to Groups, have a set of Registry metadata. However, unlike a Group, which only has Registry metadata, each Resource MAY also have a secondary domain-specific "document" associated with it. For example, a "schema" Resource might have a "schema document" as its "document". This specification places no restriction on the type of content stored in the Resource's document. Additionally, Resources (unlike Groups) MAY be versioned.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Design / Design: Data Retrieval Issues

requirements.text: In general, if a server is unable to retrieve all of the data intended to be sent in a response, then an error ([data_retrieval_error](./spec.md#data_retrieval_error)) MUST be generated and the request rejected without any changes being made. However, it is permissible for a server to attempt some creative processing. For example, if while processing a query the server can only retrieve half of the entities to be returned at the current point in time, then it could return those with an indication of there being more (via use of a [pagination](../pagination/spec.md) type of specification). Then during the next query request it could return the remainder of the data - or an error if it is still not available to retrieve the data. Note that if an entity is to be sent, then it MUST be serialized in its entirety (all attributes, and requested child entities) or an error MUST be generated.
