source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `usage`

requirements.text: - MUST contain only the following possible values: - "subscriber" - "consumer" - "producer"

review.note: Exact native role strings are accepted; unknown, empty and case-distinct role names or non-string members reject with invalid_attribute at /usage. The complete ordered native-role matrix verifies singleton acceptance independently of protocol.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `usage`

requirements.text: - MUST be an array of at least one value.

review.note: The public usage validator rejects empty arrays and every non-array JSON kind. Singleton native roles are accepted; duplicate and oversized combinations are checked separately by the exhaustive role matrix.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `usage`

requirements.text: - MUST declare exactly one usage value, except for the single combination permitted below.

review.note: All ordered one-, two- and three-role combinations are checked across qualifying, nonqualifying, case-distinct and aliased protocols. Only native singletons or the distinct consumer/subscriber pair on qualifying protocols pass; authored order and protocol casing are retained.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `usage`

requirements.text: - MUST NOT combine `producer` with any other value.

review.note: The ordered native-role matrix rejects producer combined with either other role, duplicates or all three roles on every tested protocol. A producer singleton remains accepted.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `usage`

requirements.text: - MUST NOT declare all three values.

review.note: Every ordered three-role combination rejects at /usage, including all six permutations of the three distinct roles and repeated-role arrays. The same test independently accepts the permitted smaller combinations.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `usage`

requirements.text: - MAY declare `["subscriber", "consumer"]` only when the protocol is `MQTT/3.1.1`, `MQTT/5.0`, `AMQP/1.0`, or `NATS`. In these protocols a single client connection both establishes subscription interest and receives the resulting messages, so the two roles are served by one protocol interface and one endpoint contract.

review.note: Both role orders pass for the four declared protocols, case-insensitive selectors and the specification's MQTT/AMQP default-version aliases. Unknown versions and missing or non-string protocols reject mixed roles. This checks declaration semantics, not establishment of an actual shared network connection.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `usage`

requirements.text: - MUST NOT declare `["subscriber", "consumer"]` for `HTTP` or `KAFKA` endpoints. In those protocols the two roles are distinct interfaces and MUST be modeled as separate Endpoint resources.

review.note: HTTP and KAFKA reject both orders of the consumer/subscriber pair regardless of protocol casing. Each singleton remains valid. The Kestrel test also proves that changing a valid mixed-role MQTT endpoint to HTTP fails without changing its stored protocol, usage or epoch.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `usage`

requirements.text: - Endpoints that jointly describe more than one role SHOULD be declared separately and correlated with a shared `channel` value.

review.note: The native role validator enforces the permitted combinations, and channel remains available as opaque correlation metadata. Whether independently declared endpoints describe one real multi-role service and should share a channel is a producer modeling decision.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `channel`

requirements.text: - Description: A string that can be used to correlate Endpoints. Any Endpoints within an instance of an Endpoint Registry that share the same non-empty `channel` value MUST have some relationship. This specification does not define that relationship or the specific values used in this property. However, it is expected that the `usage` value in combination with this `channel` property will provide some information to help determine the relationship.

review.note: Channel values retain their exact nonempty strings without a registry-invented relationship or comparison algorithm. Establishing an actual relationship between endpoints sharing a value requires producer semantics, which the source deliberately does not define.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `channel`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

review.note: Channel is optional. Its absence survives materialization without adding a generated channel or inferred relationship.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `channel`

requirements.text: - When specified, the value MUST be a non-empty string.

review.note: A supplied channel must be a nonempty string. Invalid native kinds and the empty string reject at /channel; spaces and punctuation remain accepted because the source defines no narrower syntax.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `envelope`

requirements.text: - MUST be a non-empty case-insensitive string of the form `<SPEC>[/<VERSION>]`, where `<SPEC>` is the non-empty string name of the specification that defines the Resource. An OPTIONAL `<VERSION>` value SHOULD be included if there are multiple versions of the specification available.

review.note: Envelope selectors require a nonempty specification name and a nonempty version when a slash is supplied. Unversioned names and opaque version text remain permitted and retain authored casing; no closed specification vocabulary or version syntax is introduced.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `envelope`

requirements.text: - If a `<VERSION>` is specified at the Group level, all Resources within that Group MUST have a `<VERSION>` value that is at least as precise as its Group, and MUST NOT expand it. For example, if a Group had a `envelope` value of `myspec`, then Resources within that Group can have `envelope` values of `myspec` or `myspec/1.0`. However, if a Group has a value of `myspec/1.0`, it would be invalid for a Resource to have a value of `myspec/2.0` or just `myspec`. Additionally, if a Group does not have an `envelope` attribute, then there are no constraints on its Resources' `envelope` attributes.

review.note: Group-to-Message envelope checks enforce specification identity and version precision, including component boundaries rather than a raw string prefix. Public consumer and engine tests reject broadening or incompatible versions and accept a permitted refinement.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `envelopeoptions`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

review.note: Envelope options can be omitted independently of the optional envelope selector. Empty and extension option objects remain intact; CloudEvents-specific declarations are checked only for that selected envelope.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `envelopeoptions` / `CloudEvents/1.0`

requirements.text: - `mode` : indicates whether the CloudEvent will use `binary` or `structured` [mode](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md#message). When specified, its value MUST be one of: `binary` or `structured`, case sensitive. When not specified, the endpoint is indicating that either mode is acceptable.

review.note: CloudEvents mode is optional and its values are the exact strings binary and structured. Case variants and non-string kinds reject; omission is preserved rather than rewritten as a default mode.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `envelopeoptions` / `CloudEvents/1.0`

requirements.text: - `format` : indicates the format of the CloudEvent when sent in `structured` mode. This attribute MUST NOT be specified when `mode` is `binary`. The value used MUST match the expected content type of the message (e.g. for HTTP the `Content-Type` header value).

review.note: Binary mode rejects format, and declared structured-format media types must agree with a declared HTTP Content-Type. Matching the actual runtime message representation remains an envelope_content_type deferred check; declaration agreement alone does not establish the compound runtime obligation.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocol`

requirements.text: - Description: The transport or application protocol used by the endpoint. This specification defines a set of common protocol names that MUST be used for respective protocol endpoints, but implementations MAY define and use additional protocol names.

review.note: Predefined protocol selectors and aliases are recognized case-insensitively; extension selectors retain their exact strings and a deferred protocol contract. Confirming that an advertised live endpoint actually speaks the named protocol requires provider/runtime evidence.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocol`

requirements.text: Predefined protocols SHOULD be referred to by name and version as `<NAME>/<VERSION>`. The version number format is determined by the protocol specification's usage of versions. If the version is not specified, the default version of the protocol is assumed. For AMQP and MQTT, see the list below. For others, refer to the protocol specifications.

review.note: Canonical protocol interpretation maps the unversioned AMQP and MQTT names to their specified defaults without rewriting authored selectors. Supported explicit versions keep their distinct protocol semantics.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocol`

requirements.text: - "AMQP/1.0" - Use the [AMQP 1.0][AMQP 1.0] protocol. MAY be shortened to "AMQP". AMQP draft versions before 1.0 (e.g. 0.9) are *not* AMQP.

review.note: AMQP and AMQP/1.0 resolve to the same predefined contract. Unsupported pre-1.0 selectors remain extension protocols rather than acquiring AMQP 1.0 validation or defaults.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocol`

requirements.text: All messages inside an Endpoint MUST use this same protocol.

review.note: Explicit child protocols must agree with the Endpoint's effective protocol, including case-insensitive predefined aliases. Public engine checks reject incompatible creation and reverse mutations through borrowed Messages atomically; unbound child metadata remains usable within the parent's contract.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocol`

requirements.text: - MUST be a non-empty case-insensitive string.

review.note: Supplied protocol selectors reject empty strings and invalid native kinds while retaining exact authored casing. Consumer access recognizes predefined names case-insensitively and preserves extension names.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocol`

requirements.text: - SHOULD follow the naming convention `<NAME>/<VERSION>`, whereby `<NAME>` is the name of the protocol and `<VERSION>` is the version of the protocol.

review.note: The naming convention remains a recommendation rather than a closed enum or mandatory version grammar. Unversioned extension names and opaque nonempty version strings remain representable.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocoloptions`

requirements.text: - Description: Configuration details of the endpoint related to the protocol used to transmit the messages. An endpoint MAY be defined without detailed configuration. In this case, the endpoint is considered to be "abstract". For per-protocol option definitions, see [Protocol Options](#protocol-options).

review.note: An Endpoint can remain abstract without protocol options. Authored admission preserves that omission; consumer materialization reports the missing address as deferred rather than acquiring or inventing one.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocoloptions`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

review.note: Protocol options are optional. Authored validation accepts their absence without inserting defaults; consumer default interpretation is separate from stored metadata.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocoloptions` / `protocoloptions.endpoints`

requirements.text: - Description: An array of objects where each object describes one network address at which clients can communicate with the endpoint. The object MAY contain extension attributes that can be used by clients to determine which address to use, or to configure access to the specific address. Whether the address identifies a network host or links directly to a resource managed by the network host is protocol specific.

review.note: Address entries retain extension attributes and authored preference order. Consumer validation interprets known address fields without replacing extension metadata or contacting the advertised endpoint.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocoloptions` / `protocoloptions.endpoints`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

review.note: The endpoint address array is optional. Abstract definitions materialize with an explicit endpoint_address deferred check instead of a fabricated address.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocoloptions` / `protocoloptions.endpoints`

requirements.text: - Each object MUST carry the endpoint address in the attribute that the endpoint's protocol defines for that purpose. Of the protocols defined in this specification, `HTTP`, `AMQP/1.0`, `MQTT/3.1.1`, `MQTT/5.0`, and `NATS` use a `uri` attribute holding a valid, absolute URI (URL), and `KAFKA` uses a non-empty `bootstrap.servers` attribute. A protocol defined outside of this specification MAY define a different addressing attribute.

review.note: Consumer materialization requires protocol-specific address fields on supplied entries: absolute network URIs for the five URI protocols and nonempty Kafka bootstrap lists. Invalid shapes and malformed addresses reject at their exact paths; external protocols can retain their own addressing fields.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocoloptions` / `protocoloptions.authorization`

requirements.text: - Description: OPTIONAL authorization configuration details of the endpoint. Each entry describes one authorization option that the endpoint accepts; a client selects one of them. When specified, each entry MUST provide sufficient metadata for clients to select the authorization mechanism and discover where authorization is obtained. Runtime credentials and deployment-specific values are expected to be supplied separately through external configuration. The attribute names below MUST be used as defined. Additional endpoint-specific extension attributes MAY be added.

review.note: Known authorization member kinds, optional selectors and extension metadata are checked without acquiring credentials or discovery documents. Every nonempty alternative produces authorization_configuration deferral. Actual selection and sufficiency of provider-specific discovery metadata remain consumer obligations; these declarations alone do not prove them.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocoloptions` / `protocoloptions.authorization`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

review.note: Authorization is optional. Existing concrete declarations without authorization remain materializable; an explicit empty alternatives array is also preserved without adding a required selector or credential.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocoloptions` / `protocoloptions.authorization`

requirements.text: - MUST be an array of objects if present.

review.note: All non-array native JSON kinds reject for authorization; every non-object array member rejects at its indexed path. Valid alternatives retain their order and extension members.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocoloptions` / `protocoloptions.authorization`

requirements.text: - MUST only be used for authorization configuration.

review.note: Recognized credential carriers are rejected by consumer materialization, while provider-specific authorization configuration is retained and explicitly deferred. An arbitrary extension's semantic purpose cannot be established from its JSON representation; application confirmation remains necessary.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocoloptions` / `protocoloptions.authorization`

requirements.text: - MUST NOT be used for credential configuration.

review.note: Consumer materialization rejects recognized credential fields, URI user information, credential query keys and declared HTTP carriers. Supplied values do not leak through diagnostics. Unknown extension payloads cannot be proven credential-free generically, so the complete credential prohibition remains an application obligation.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocoloptions` / `protocoloptions.authorization` / `protocoloptions.authorization.type`

requirements.text: - Description: The type of the authorization configuration. The value SHOULD be one of the following:

review.note: The listed authorization types are recommendations rather than a closed enum. Standard and vendor selectors are preserved; an absent type is permitted when extension discovery metadata supplies the alternative.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocoloptions` / `protocoloptions.authorization` / `protocoloptions.authorization.type`

requirements.text: - `OAuth2`: [OAuth 2.0][RFC6749] authorization is used. The [`authorityuri`](#protocoloptionsauthorizationauthorityuri) SHOULD reference authorization server metadata as defined by [RFC 8414][RFC8414].

review.note: OAuth2 metadata can identify an issuer or discovery location without local acquisition. Verification that a selected authority actually provides RFC8414 metadata remains a consumer obligation and is reported as authorization_configuration deferral.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocoloptions` / `protocoloptions.authorization` / `protocoloptions.authorization.type`

requirements.text: - `Plain`: The client uses a username with a plaintext password for authentication and authorization. For HTTP, see the [HTTP options](#http-options) `plainscheme`, `plainusernamefield`, and `plainpasswordfield`; for other protocols, equivalent transport-specific options MAY be defined as protocol extensions.

review.note: Plain authorization configuration and HTTP carrier names are supported separately from credentials. Equivalent non-HTTP extension semantics and actual username/password authentication require provider-specific consumer integration.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocoloptions` / `protocoloptions.authorization` / `protocoloptions.authorization.type`

requirements.text: - `SASL`: The client uses a [SASL][RFC4422] authentication mechanism. The [`mechanism`](#protocoloptionsauthorizationmechanism) attribute SHOULD be provided when this type is selected.

review.note: SASL mechanism metadata is permitted only with exact type SASL. Omission remains valid because the source recommends rather than requires a mechanism; selecting and negotiating the actual SASL mechanism is deferred to the consumer.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocoloptions` / `protocoloptions.authorization` / `protocoloptions.authorization.type`

requirements.text: - `APIKey`: The client uses an API key for authentication and authorization. For HTTP, see the [HTTP options](#http-options) `apikeyname` and `apikeyin`; for other protocols, equivalent carrier-specific options MAY be defined as protocol extensions.

review.note: APIKey configuration is distinct from credential material and HTTP carriers are recognized during credential rejection. Non-HTTP carrier extensions and actual key provisioning or authentication remain consumer responsibilities.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocoloptions` / `protocoloptions.authorization` / `protocoloptions.authorization.type`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

review.note: The type selector is optional and is not synthesized. An alternative can retain vendor selection metadata without type while still reporting provider-specific verification as deferred.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocoloptions` / `protocoloptions.authorization` / `protocoloptions.authorization.type`

requirements.text: - MUST be a non-empty string if used.

review.note: When supplied, type must be a nonempty native JSON string. All other JSON kinds and the empty string reject at the exact member path; standard and extension strings are retained.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocoloptions` / `protocoloptions.authorization` / `protocoloptions.authorization.mechanism`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

review.note: A SASL alternative may omit mechanism. Materialization preserves the omission and does not invent a default mechanism.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocoloptions` / `protocoloptions.authorization` / `protocoloptions.authorization.mechanism`

requirements.text: - MUST be a non-empty string if used.

review.note: A supplied mechanism must be a nonempty string, independently of the conditional SASL type rule. Empty and non-string values reject at the mechanism path.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocoloptions` / `protocoloptions.authorization` / `protocoloptions.authorization.mechanism`

requirements.text: - MUST only be used when `protocoloptions.authorization.type` is `SASL`.

review.note: Mechanism is accepted only with exact type SASL. Missing, Plain and case-distinct sasl selectors reject when mechanism is supplied; mechanism is not made mandatory.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocoloptions` / `protocoloptions.authorization` / `protocoloptions.authorization.resourceuri`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

review.note: The resource URI is optional. Valid alternatives without resourceuri retain the omission; no resource identity is inferred from a different member.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocoloptions` / `protocoloptions.authorization` / `protocoloptions.authorization.resourceuri`

requirements.text: - MUST be a non-empty URI if used.

review.note: A supplied resourceuri must be a nonempty URI reference under the registry URI type. Empty strings, invalid native kinds and malformed references reject; URNs and relative references are retained without acquisition.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocoloptions` / `protocoloptions.authorization` / `protocoloptions.authorization.authorityuri`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

review.note: The authority URI is optional. Alternatives without authorityuri remain valid when their extension metadata or selected type supplies the declaration; actual discovery sufficiency remains deferred.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocoloptions` / `protocoloptions.authorization` / `protocoloptions.authorization.authorityuri`

requirements.text: - MUST be a non-empty URI if used.

review.note: A supplied authorityuri must be a nonempty URI reference. Malformed references and every invalid native kind reject at the exact member path. Relative discovery references remain data and are not retrieved.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocoloptions` / `protocoloptions.deployed`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

review.note: Deployment metadata is optional for predefined and extension protocols. Omission is preserved in both authored and resolved representations while the consumer accessor supplies the normative true default.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocoloptions` / `protocoloptions.deployed`

requirements.text: - If present, MUST be either `true` or `false`, case-sensitive.

review.note: Only native true and false values are accepted for deployed. Null, numbers, strings of either casing, arrays and objects reject at /protocoloptions/deployed without coercion.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocoloptions` / `protocoloptions.deployed`

requirements.text: - When not specified, the default value MUST be `true`.

review.note: Absent deployed is interpreted as true whether protocoloptions is omitted or empty. Explicit false remains false; neither interpretation rewrites the declaration or constitutes a runtime liveness check.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `messages`

requirements.text: Endpoints are supersets of [message definition groups](../message/spec.md#message-definition-groups) and MAY contain inlined messages. See [Message Definitions](../message/spec.md#message-definitions).

review.note: Inline Message definitions remain available directly within an Endpoint alongside explicitly supplied referenced collections. The consumer does not fetch unknown groups or invent missing definitions.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `messages`

requirements.text: When this specification, and the [message specification](../message/spec.md), are used with specifications such as [CloudEvents](https://cloudevents.io), where a semantically unique identifier is used in a runtime message (e.g. CloudEvent's `type` attribute), it is STRONGLY RECOMMENDED that the `messageid` values of the message definitions for an Endpoint match that unique identifier and therefore be unique across all messages within the `messages` collection and the messages referenced by the `messagegroups` attribute. This will allow for an easy "lookup" from an incoming runtime message to its related message definition.

review.note: Exact Message ID lookup is available across inline and supplied referenced collections. Ambiguity and incomplete collections fail explicitly; correspondence between an actual runtime event type and a producer-chosen Message ID remains a producer integration obligation.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `messages`

requirements.text: Implementations MAY choose to generate an error if they detect duplicate `messageid` values across the `messages` collection message definitions and the `messagegroups` referenced message definitions, if that is the desired constraint for their users.

review.note: Duplicate IDs remain legal by default, but ambiguous aggregate selection fails. The explicit RejectDuplicateMessageIds policy rejects them during materialization without silently choosing the first definition.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options

requirements.text: For each protocol specified in the following sections there is a table that describes the set of protocol-specific options and the roles (Producer, Consumer, Subscriber) to which each option applies. All protocol options are OPTIONAL.

review.note: Protocol options are optional and defaults are consumer interpretations rather than injected fields. More specific conditional requirements, such as a Kafka consumer's group, remain enforced separately; descriptive role cells do not create extra prohibitions.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options

requirements.text: The role applicability is descriptive: it guides clients on how to interpret metadata. Where a rule below is stated with MUST, MUST NOT, or REQUIRED, it is a conformance requirement of this specification, and a client evaluating the metadata MUST treat a violation as an error. A Registry server is not obligated to check these rules.

review.note: Bounded consumer evaluation rejects the explicit declaration violations exercised by protocol tests, while authored storage can preserve consumer-only violations. Applying every protocol option to an actual connection remains outside this metadata component and is not established by these checks.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options

requirements.text: - `✓`: The option applies to that role. Clients acting in that role SHOULD apply the option semantics.

review.note: Role-table cells guide consumer interpretation and are not an admission allowlist. Native option types and explicit cross-option rules are checked, but actual client application of all role-relative protocol settings needs provider integration.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options

requirements.text: Any string value of any protocol option MAY contain placeholders expressed with the [RFC6570][RFC6570] Level 1 URI Template expression syntax, for example `orders/{tenantid}/events`. This applies to plain string values, to the string items of arrays, and to the keys and values of maps, and it also applies to the `uri` values of [`protocoloptions.endpoints`](#protocoloptionsendpoints). Placeholders are resolved out-of-band by the client; this specification does not define how the values are supplied. When the same placeholder name occurs in more than one value of the same endpoint, all of its occurrences MUST resolve to the same value.

review.note: Level-1 expansion uses one explicit string binding per exact variable name across URI values, array strings and map keys or values. Unsupported operators, undefined or typed bindings and key collisions reject; structural record member names remain literal.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / HTTP options

requirements.text: The [endpoint URIs](#protocoloptionsendpoints) for "HTTP" endpoints MUST be valid HTTP URIs using the "http" or "https" scheme as defined in [HTTP Message Format].

review.note: HTTP consumer addresses require an absolute network URI with http or https scheme. Wrong schemes, relative paths and malformed lexical forms reject after template expansion; accepted addresses retain their spelling.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / HTTP options

requirements.text: - An HTTP Endpoint MUST declare exactly one `usage` value and therefore MUST represent exactly one of the three roles above.

review.note: Every ordered role combination on HTTP and case-distinct http accepts only native singletons. Invalid combinations reject at /usage independently of protocol options.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / HTTP options

requirements.text: - An HTTP Endpoint MUST NOT declare `["subscriber", "consumer"]`.

review.note: Both consumer/subscriber orders reject for HTTP. A stored mixed-role MQTT endpoint cannot be patched to HTTP without changing its roles; failure preserves its previous state.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / HTTP options

requirements.text: - A subscription manager, a delivery target, and a pull consumer that belong to the same logical channel MUST be declared as separate Endpoint resources and SHOULD be correlated with a shared `channel` value.

review.note: HTTP declarations cannot combine the three interfaces into one usage array. Whether a subscription manager, delivery target and pull endpoint describe the same deployed channel, and should be correlated, requires producer modeling information beyond the registry declarations.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / HTTP options

requirements.text: | `apikeyin` | enum: `header`, `query`, default `header` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Placement of API key metadata when `authorization.type` is `APIKey`. `header` SHOULD be used; `query` SHOULD only be used when header placement is not possible. |

review.note: HTTP API-key placement defaults to header; exact header and query enum values are accepted. Whether header placement is impossible and query is justified is a deployment decision that this metadata validator cannot establish.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / HTTP options

requirements.text: These options only define protocol-level placement and naming metadata. Credential values (API keys, usernames, passwords) MUST NOT be stored in endpoint metadata and MUST be supplied out-of-band.

review.note: Known credential carriers are rejected by consumer materialization and diagnostics do not echo supplied credentials. The caller must supply runtime credentials separately; arbitrary extension payloads cannot be proven free of credentials by generic metadata validation.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / AMQP options

requirements.text: The [endpoint URIs](#protocoloptionsendpoints) for "AMQP" endpoints MUST be valid AMQP URIs using the "amqp" or "amqps" scheme. If the path portion of the URI is present, it MUST be a valid AMQP node name according to [AMQP Addressing Version 1.0].

review.note: AMQP addresses require amqp or amqps URIs with lexical validation. Container-specific node-name and terminus resolution remain explicitly deferred, including when a node option overrides the URI path; syntactic acceptance alone does not complete the compound addressing obligation.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / AMQP options

requirements.text: An AMQP Endpoint MAY declare `["subscriber", "consumer"]`, because a single AMQP receiving link both establishes interest in the source node and carries the resulting transfers. When it does, the `subscriber` role refers to the establishment of the link with the node as source and the `consumer` role refers to the transfers over that link.

review.note: Both consumer/subscriber role orders are permitted for AMQP and AMQP/1.0, including case-insensitive spellings. Producer combinations remain invalid. This disposition covers the allowed declaration, not establishment of a receiving link.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / MQTT options

requirements.text: The [endpoint URIs](#protocoloptionsendpoints) for "MQTT" endpoints MUST be valid MQTT URIs using the (informal) "mqtt" or "mqtts" scheme. If the path portion of the URI is present, it MUST be a valid MQTT topic name as described by [MQTT 3.1.1] and [MQTT 5.0]. The informal schemes "tcp" (plain TCP/1883), "ssl" (TLS TCP/8883), and "wss" (Websockets/443) MAY also be used, but MUST NOT have a path.

review.note: MQTT URI paths are decoded once and checked as concrete topics. MQTT/MQTTS schemes permit such paths; TCP/SSL/WSS schemes reject every path, including a trailing slash. Malformed escapes, invalid UTF-8 and wildcard destinations reject.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / MQTT options

requirements.text: - `topic` MUST be a concrete MQTT topic name. It MUST NOT contain the `+` or `#` wildcard characters, since a wildcard is not a valid publish destination.

review.note: Concrete MQTT topic names reject either wildcard, empty values and invalid string boundaries. Valid publish topics remain accepted without interpreting them as subscription filters.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / MQTT options

requirements.text: - `topicfilter` MAY contain the `+` and `#` wildcard characters as defined by [MQTT 3.1.1] and [MQTT 5.0].

review.note: MQTT filters accept complete-level plus wildcards and a complete final hash wildcard. Invalid placements reject; literal option values are not expanded a second time when a shared filter is derived.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / MQTT options

requirements.text: - An MQTT Endpoint MUST NOT declare both `topic` and `topicfilter`.

review.note: A resolved MQTT definition cannot declare both topic and topicfilter. Authored storage may retain such a declaration because this is an explicit consumer evaluation requirement, not a mandatory server check.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / MQTT options

requirements.text: - An MQTT Endpoint MAY declare `["subscriber", "consumer"]`, because a single MQTT connection both sends the `SUBSCRIBE` packet and receives the resulting `PUBLISH` packets.

review.note: MQTT 3.1.1 and 5.0 declarations accept the distinct consumer/subscriber pair in either order; the unversioned alias follows MQTT 5.0. No producer role can join that pair.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / MQTT options

requirements.text: - `sharedsubscriptiongroup` MUST only be present when `topicfilter` is also present.

review.note: MQTT 5 sharedsubscriptiongroup requires topicfilter. Missing filters reject at the group option path, while a valid literal group and filter produce the derived subscription filter.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / MQTT options

requirements.text: - The value of `sharedsubscriptiongroup` is the bare group name. It MUST NOT include the `$share/` prefix and MUST NOT contain the `/` character.

review.note: Shared groups reject the reserved dollar-share prefix and every slash instead of accepting an already-assembled shared filter. Empty and wildcard-bearing group names also reject under the referenced MQTT rules.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / MQTT options

requirements.text: - When `sharedsubscriptiongroup` is present, a client MUST send the subscription as the topic filter `$share/{sharedsubscriptiongroup}/{topicfilter}`, where `{sharedsubscriptiongroup}` and `{topicfilter}` are the literal values of those two options.

review.note: The consumer helper derives the exact dollar-share/group/filter value from resolved literal options and checks its byte budget. Sending that value in an actual MQTT subscription remains the caller's protocol operation, not a registry or metadata-materialization action.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / KAFKA options

requirements.text: For `KAFKA` endpoints, the [endpoint addresses](#protocoloptionsendpoints) MUST be carried in `bootstrap.servers` as an array of client bootstrap addresses. Each entry MUST use the `host:port` format without a scheme. The listener-style `uri` format is not an alternative addressing field for a `KAFKA` endpoint.

review.note: Resolved Kafka bootstrap values accept only scheme-free host:port entries, including bracketed IPv6 and inclusive port boundaries. Listener prefixes reject rather than being stripped or converted into a security-mapping deferral; uri is not an alternative field. Authored templates remain storable and are checked after explicit expansion. This replaces the incompatible historical listener interpretation without changing pinned source text.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / KAFKA options

requirements.text: - A `subscriber` Kafka Endpoint describes the creation and configuration of a consumer group as an act of registering interest. It MUST NOT declare `consumergroup`, since the group is the resource being established rather than a group to be joined.

review.note: A Kafka subscriber declaration rejects consumergroup even when other options are absent. It does not silently reinterpret the declaration as joining an existing group or create a group at a broker.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / KAFKA options

requirements.text: - A `consumer` Kafka Endpoint describes joining an existing consumer group. It MUST declare `consumergroup` with a non-empty value.

review.note: A Kafka consumer requires a nonempty consumergroup, including abstract definitions without protocoloptions. A valid exact group identifier is preserved in the resulting metadata.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / KAFKA options

requirements.text: - A Kafka Endpoint MUST NOT declare `["subscriber", "consumer"]`. The two roles MUST be declared as separate Endpoint resources and SHOULD be correlated with a shared `channel` value.

review.note: The native Kafka role rule rejects the combined consumer/subscriber array in both orders. Publishing complete separate deployed interfaces and choosing a shared channel require producer modeling evidence beyond rejection of one invalid declaration.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / KAFKA options

requirements.text: - `autooffsetreset` and `enableautocommit` describe group-based consumption. They MUST NOT be used on a `producer` or `subscriber` Endpoint.

review.note: Kafka producer and subscriber declarations reject autooffsetreset or enableautocommit when present, including an explicit false boolean. Existing-group consumers can retain valid reset and auto-commit options.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / KAFKA options

requirements.text: - `autooffsetreset` expresses only the reset behavior when no valid committed offset exists. A concrete starting offset or a starting timestamp is runtime consumer state, not endpoint metadata, and MUST NOT be expressed through this option.

review.note: Autooffsetreset accepts only earliest, latest or none. It cannot carry a concrete offset or timestamp through a numeric value or an unrecognized string; the native enum remains distinct from runtime consumer state.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / NATS options

requirements.text: The [endpoint URIs](#protocoloptionsendpoints) for "NATS" endpoints MUST be valid NATS URIs as described by [NATS]. The scheme MUST be "nats" or "tls" or "ws" and the URI MUST include a port number, e.g. `nats://<HOST>:<PORT>` or `tls://<HOST>:<PORT>`.

review.note: NATS addresses require nats, tls or ws scheme and an explicit port in the supported network range. Missing ports, zero or oversized ports and unsupported wss addresses reject; IPv6 and boundary ports are covered.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / NATS options

requirements.text: - `subject` MUST be a concrete NATS subject. It MUST NOT contain the `*` or `>` wildcard tokens, since a wildcard is not a valid publish destination.

review.note: Concrete NATS subjects reject wildcard tokens, empty components and whitespace. Valid publish subjects remain distinct from subscription filters.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / NATS options

requirements.text: - `subjectfilter` MAY contain the `*` and `>` wildcard tokens as defined by [NATS].

review.note: NATS filters accept whole-token star wildcards and a whole final greater-than wildcard. Embedded or nonfinal wildcards reject rather than being interpreted as literal publish subjects.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / NATS options

requirements.text: - `queuegroup` MUST only be present when `subjectfilter` is also present.

review.note: A supplied NATS queuegroup requires a subjectfilter and a nonempty group name. The valid group and filter remain exact metadata; no subscription is established.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / NATS options

requirements.text: - A NATS Endpoint MUST NOT declare both `subject` and `subjectfilter`.

review.note: NATS consumer evaluation rejects a simultaneous subject and subjectfilter declaration at the filter path, independently of descriptive role-table applicability.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / NATS options

requirements.text: - A NATS Endpoint MAY declare `["subscriber", "consumer"]`, because a single Core NATS connection both registers the subscription interest and receives the resulting messages.

review.note: NATS declarations accept the distinct subscriber/consumer pair in either order. The permission is implemented as a metadata rule without treating it as proof of an established Core NATS connection.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Overview / Message Metadata

requirements.text: A `message` definition MAY contain any combination of `envelope`, `protocol`, and data payload declarations. A payload-only declaration can be useful if messages are sent through varying protocols without a fixed envelope model and are distinguished by content-type (including parameters) or even only through whether payload schema definitions match an incoming message.

review.note: Envelope, protocol and payload declarations are independently optional and can be combined. ValidateMessageMetadata requires option objects only when the corresponding selector is present; payload-only definitions remain valid. MessageEnvelopeRulesRequireMetadataWithoutRequiringAnEnvelope and BindingPrecedenceDoesNotInventAnImplicitConcreteProtocol cover unbound/payload-only/envelope/protocol/both cases. Runtime matching against application payloads is distinct from storage and materialization. Full qualification remains pending.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Overview / Reusing Message Definitions

requirements.text: The `basemessage` attribute, a URI-typed reference to another message definition, enables such reuse scenarios. Any message definition MAY refer to another message definition as its base, which effects a copy of the base message’s definitions into the message that defines it. The mechanism is transitive, which means that `basemessage` relationships MUST be resolved recursively as long as they do not result in circular references.

review.note: Message reuse introduction defines optional basemessage inheritance and recursive resolution without cycles. Read with normative basemessage section at lines 589-634: server stores and admits references without acquisition; consumer materialization follows the caller-authorized source chain. MessageDefinitionMaterializer and MessageMaterializationTraversalTests provide explicit local/external traversal, transitive composition, direct/transitive/alias-cycle handling and unavailable-source outcomes. This is a client materialization obligation, not a server mandate to fetch all bases. Full per-requirement qualification remains pending.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Overview / Message Definition Matching

requirements.text: - Use of CloudEvents is RECOMMENDED as it will provide well-defined metadata that will appear in each Message to help differentiate Message definitions.

review.note: Read within Message Definition Matching, which explicitly does not mandate a matching mechanism and permits deviation. CloudEvents is supported but not mandatory: MessageEnvelopeRulesRequireMetadataWithoutRequiringAnEnvelope and BindingPrecedenceDoesNotInventAnImplicitConcreteProtocol admit envelope-only, protocol-only and payload-only definitions. This library stores/materializes definitions; matching incoming application messages is a consumer responsibility. No recommendation is converted to a registry admission requirement.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Overview / Message Definition Matching

requirements.text: - Message definitions SHOULD have a `messageid` value that is the same as the CloudEvents' `type` context attribute defined for that Message. This will allow for an exact mapping from the incoming Message's `type` attribute to its related Message definition.

review.note: Read with the explicit permission to deviate from matching recommendations. Resource identity and authored CloudEvents type constraints are not rewritten or forced equal by storage/materialization. TypedCloudEventsPropertyValuesRetainTheirActualJsonTypesAndNullPresence and ImpliedCloudEventsRequirementsAndPayloadReferencesBecomeExplicitConstraints retain declarations independently of messageid. Selecting definitions for incoming messages remains consumer policy; no mandatory matching algorithm or identity rewrite is inferred.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Overview / Message Definition Matching

requirements.text: - Message Resource types SHOULD be defined with a `maxversions` of `1`. This eliminates the need for each incoming Message to include some unique Version discriminator.

review.note: Read as a model-author recommendation, with deviation permitted in the following paragraph. The active packaged Message Resource has maxversions 1, while custom compatible models remain subject to Core version behavior and explicit author configuration. This does not authorize rewriting a caller model to force one Version or selecting an incoming-message Version without a discriminator. Core lifecycle and full model/package evidence remain separately qualified.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Overview / Message Definition Matching

requirements.text: - Modifications to Message definitions SHOULD NOT result in "on the wire" changes to the resulting messages as that could break existing systems. Rather, new Message definitions SHOULD be created, with new `type` and `messageid` values, and referenced through the use of the `deprecated` attribute.

review.note: Read as application/model-author evolution guidance, not a prohibition on registry metadata updates. The library does not generate application wire messages and cannot infer whether a changed constraint breaks deployed consumers. Atomic declaration patch/restart tests preserve explicit storage semantics; authors remain responsible for assigning replacement identities and deprecation references when changing wire contracts. Library API backward compatibility is distinct from this specification recommendation.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Overview / Message Definition Matching

requirements.text: Implementations and Registry model authors MAY deviate from these recommendations; however, they are then responsible for defining the mechanisms by which a unique Message definition is matched to incoming messages.

review.note: The library preserves explicit models and definitions rather than imposing CloudEvents/type identity or an incoming-message matching algorithm. BindingPrecedenceDoesNotInventAnImplicitConcreteProtocol and MessageEnvelopeRulesRequireMetadataWithoutRequiringAnEnvelope cover alternate definition forms. An application deviating from the preceding recommendations must define its own unique-definition matching policy; storage/materialization does not claim to implement that consumer runtime policy.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Groups

requirements.text: All message definitions MUST be contained in a group. A message group can be formed for many reasons. At a minimum, the group will be an access control boundary in many implementations of this specification even though none is mandated.

review.note: Read with Message Groups and the Core Resource path model. Message Resources are owned by modeled Groups; public Message tests create them through /messagegroups/{id}/messages/{id}, including atomic implicit Group creation. Endpoint composition also owns Message Resources under its modeled Group. Group contract tests enforce selectors without claiming that every Group is an access-control boundary; authorization policy and full Core path admission qualification remain separate. No registry-wide ungrouped Message collection is introduced.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Notations and Terminology / Notational Conventions

requirements.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2119).

review.note: RFC 2119 terminology defines interpretation of normative keywords, not a separate interoperable operation or behavior to implement.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Notations and Terminology / Notational Conventions

requirements.text: For clarity, OPTIONAL attributes (specification-defined and extensions) are OPTIONAL for clients to use, but the servers' responsibility will vary. Server-unknown extension attributes MUST be silently stored in the backing datastore. Specification-defined attributes and server-known extension attributes MUST generate an error if the corresponding feature is not supported or enabled. However, as with all attributes, if accepting the attribute results in a bad state (such as exceeding a size limit or resulting in a security issue), then the server MAY choose to reject the request.

review.note: Read as a compound Core admission obligation, not a blanket permission to ignore unsupported known features. Explicitly compatible Message models apply domain checks after Core admission; ordinary unmarked models retain Core rules. CompletionPreservesOpaquePayloadSchemasInsteadOfTreatingThemAsDeclarations proves an opaque schema is not traversed as Message declarations, and CompletionEnforcesTheExpandedOutputByteBudgetAtTheExactBoundary proves explicit size rejection. Unknown extension retention, disabled-known-feature rejection, persistence and authorization partitions require the broader Core/binding audit; those portions are not established merely by Message suite success. Keep implementation status pending.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Notations and Terminology / Notational Conventions

requirements.text: In the pseudo JSON format snippets `?` means the preceding attribute is OPTIONAL, `*` means the preceding attribute MAY appear zero or more times, and `+` means the preceding attribute MUST appear at least once. The presence of the `#` character means the remaining portion of the line is a comment. Whitespace characters in the JSON snippets are used for readability and are not normative.

review.note: Pseudo-JSON notation and explanatory whitespace conventions interpret illustrative snippets; they are not literal wire syntax or independent server behavior.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Notations and Terminology / Terminology / Envelopes and Protocols

requirements.text: This specification uses **protocol** as a selector into the protocol-specific message metadata that is defined under the `protocol.ifvalues` section of the model. When a known protocol is explicitly specified for a message definition, the `protocoloptions` section MAY contain constraints for the protocol-specific metadata.

review.note: Known protocol selectors select protocoloptions metadata through model conditional definitions; specifying protocol does not require every possible option. RequireSelectedObject and the packaged Message model supply the declaration boundary. MessageProtocolRulesRequireAnObjectAcrossBindings and MessageProtocolSelectionRequiresOptionsBeforePublishing cover all packaged bindings with empty option objects and missing-object failures. Actual transport exchange remains application-owned. Full profile/model consistency review and qualification remain unfinished.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Definition Registry Model / Message Definition Groups / `envelope` (Message Group)

requirements.text: - Description: Identifies a common, transport protocol-independent message metadata format. Message metadata envelopes are referenced by name and version as `<NAME>/<VERSION>`. This specification defines a set of common [metadata envelope names](#metadata-envelopes) that MUST be used for the given envelopes, but applications MAY define extensions for other envelopes on their own. All messages inside a group MUST use this same envelope.

review.note: Read with Message Group and Resource envelope definitions. ValidateMessageGroupMetadata and ValidateMessageStrings apply nonempty versioned selectors without rewriting case. RegistryDomainRules.Groups checks owning-group agreement, borrowed targets and reverse mutations. MessageGroupEnvelopeMustBeDeclaredByItsChildren, GroupSelectorChangesValidateExistingChildrenAndAtomicFinalValues and DomainGroupContractsValidateBorrowedMessagesAndReverseMutations provide public contract evidence. Other envelope names remain extensions; this registry does not infer transport/runtime support from a selector. Full alias/locality qualification remains separate.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Definition Registry Model / Message Definition Groups / `envelope` (Message Group)

requirements.text: - If present, MUST be a non-empty case-insensitive string.

review.note: Read with the envelope name/version definition. GroupSelectorsValidateKindsAndVersionPartsWithoutRewriting covers empty/non-string values, missing names/versions and valid authored lower-case custom envelopes; the same validator is used for Message metadata. Group relation tests compare selectors case-insensitively without rewriting metadata. Custom envelope support is not implied by syntactic admission; complete qualification remains pending.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Definition Registry Model / Message Definition Groups / `envelope` (Message Group)

requirements.text: - If present, MUST follow the naming convention `<NAME>/<VERSION>`, whereby `<NAME>` is the name of the metadata envelope and `<VERSION>` is the version of the metadata envelope.

review.note: ValidateMessageGroupMetadata uses the version-required selector validator also used by Message metadata. Empty names/versions and unversioned envelopes reject; valid authored spelling is retained. Read with the adjacent nonempty/case-insensitive rule and CloudEvents declaration requirements. MessageStringsEnforceOnlyDeclaredDomainConstraints and MessageGroupEnvelopeMustBeDeclaredByItsChildren cover the direct and public boundaries. This does not change Endpoint envelope rules or certify custom envelope implementations.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Definition Registry Model / Message Definition Groups / `protocol` (Message Group)

requirements.text: - Description: Identifies a transport protocol to be bound to for this Message. Protocols are referenced by name and version as `<NAME>/<VERSION>`. This specification defines a set of common [message protocol names](#message-protocols) that MUST be used for the given protocols, but applications MAY define extensions for other protocols on their own. All messages inside a group MUST use this same protocol.

review.note: Read with the common protocol name list and optional Resource protocol rule. Known names activate native declaration rules case-insensitively; custom names retain extension admission. Message ProtocolSelector validation rejects bare MQTT because supported incompatible versions use different options. DomainGroupContractsRejectIncompatibleChildProtocols and GroupSelectorChangesValidateExistingChildrenAndAtomicFinalValues cover owning-group consistency and atomic reverse changes. UnboundMessagesRemainUsableWithinProtocolBoundGroups captures the optional Resource selector boundary; no transport acquisition occurs. HTTP heading/name inconsistency and full borrowed-reference qualification remain explicit review work.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Definition Registry Model / Message Definition Groups / `protocol` (Message Group)

requirements.text: - If present, MUST be a non-empty case-insensitive string.

review.note: Read with the protocol naming rule. GroupSelectorsValidateKindsAndVersionPartsWithoutRewriting checks empty/non-string kinds, missing names/versions and valid authored custom/MQTT names. The common Message-specific selector helper preserves spelling, rejects bare MQTT and leaves Endpoint rules separate. Group contract tests enforce case-insensitive agreement. Syntax admission does not certify protocol runtime support or custom-version compatibility.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Definition Registry Model / Message Definition Groups / `protocol` (Message Group)

requirements.text: - If present, MUST follow the naming convention `<NAME>` or `<NAME>/<VERSION>`, whereby `<NAME>` is the name of the protocol and `<VERSION>` is the version of protocol. The version is REQUIRED if multiple, mutually incompatible versions of the protocol exist and protocol options differ between versions.

review.note: The shared Message/Message Group protocol validator now rejects unversioned MQTT without assigning guessed versions or changing Endpoint admission. MessageAndGroupMqttSelectorsRequireTheIncompatibleVersion proves exact errors; MessageProtocolSelectorVersionRulesPreserveSupportedAndCustomNames retains known versioned/custom spellings; MessageMqttVersionRuleDoesNotChangeEndpointSelectorAdmission proves scope. UnversionedMqttCannotBypassMessageOrGroupDomainAdmission removes conditional Core branches in a compatible test model and proves domain-only invalid creation/patch atomicity and restart. Unsupported custom version compatibility cannot be inferred from its name; full protocol qualification remains pending.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Definition Registry Model / Message Definitions (Message Group)

requirements.text: When [CloudEvents](https://cloudevents.io) is used for a particular message, it is RECOMMENDED that the message's `messageid` attribute be the same as the [CloudEvents `type` attribute](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md#type). Doing so makes for easier management of the meta-model by correlating the look-up value (id) of messages with their related events.

review.note: Read with Message Definition Matching recommendations and its deviation clause. Authored Message identity and CloudEvents type are preserved independently; the library does not force equality or infer wire compatibility from a metadata diff. New identities/type values and deprecation for changed wire contracts are model-author/producer responsibilities. Registry updates remain atomic and permitted; this is not a library backward-compatibility promise or a runtime matcher implementation.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Definition Registry Model / Message Definitions (Message Group) / `basemessage`

requirements.text: When the value is a relative reference (begins with `/`), it MUST be a valid XID referencing a Resource, or Version, of type `message` within the same registry. When the value is an absolute URI, it MUST point to a message definition in an external registry, but the server is not mandated to validate or resolve external references.

review.note: Compound clause separates local Registry-root XID syntax and Message Resource/Version model type from external absolute-URI target resolution. RegistryDomainRules.ValidateMessageBaseReference checks local path kinds and compatible model annotation without requiring target existence, and checks external URI syntax without target access. MissingBaseDefinitionsPublishWithoutAcquisitionOrExistenceValidation covers durable local Resource/Version and unreachable external references; InvalidLocalBaseKindsAndNonMessageTypesRejectBeforePublication covers wrong kinds/types and no events. Client LocalMessageResourceAndVersionReferencesUseTheExplicitRegistryRoot covers the explicit root rather than the definition's URL parent. Qualification remains pending.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Definition Registry Model / Message Definitions (Message Group) / `basemessage`

requirements.text: Referenced messages MAY themselves have a `basemessage` value; however, the chain of messages MUST NOT be recursive.

review.note: Recursive here means a circular base chain, not ordinary multi-level inheritance. Consumer materialization uses requested and acquired actual URI identities to reject direct, transitive and alias cycles before returning a success. UriEquivalentDirectCyclesAreRejectedBeforeAcquisition, ATransitiveCycleCannotReturnAPartialSuccess and ActualSourceIdentityDetectsAnAliasCycle cover these cases; DistinctFragmentsAreNotCollapsedByUriEquality preserves distinct fragment identities. Server external-reference admission does not acquire or validate the external chain. Per-requirement qualification remains pending.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Definition Registry Model / Message Definitions (Message Group) / `basemessage`

requirements.text: The process that a client SHOULD follow to materialize the message is to follow the `basemessage` references to the end of the chain of messages, get that message's attributes, and then walk back up the chain performing a "merge" operation of the next message's attributes. Note that if an inherited attribute is a complex type (e.g. map, object) and the overlaying attribute is scalar, then the entire inherited attribute (and nested values) are replaced by that scalar value. For complex types, the merge is "deep", meaning each level of the complex type is merged appropriately rather than it being a complete replacement of the entire complex type.

review.note: Client SHOULD traversal is ordered from the authored definition to the oldest available base, then overlays from oldest to newest. Object/map members merge deeply; a scalar overlay replaces the inherited complex value. MessageDefinitionMaterializer.Merge implements this with retained source provenance; RecursiveOverridesReplaceArraysAndScalarsWithoutLosingDuplicatesOrNull covers nested winners, scalar/complex replacement and inherited origins. Its whole-array replacement is an implementation policy, not proof that this prose fully specifies array merge semantics. Property defaults and domain completion occur after complete overlays; unavailable tails remain explicitly incomplete. Qualification remains pending.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Definition Registry Model / Message Definitions (Message Group) / `basemessage`

requirements.text: If the referenced message can not be found, whether due to a dangling reference, an unreachable external registry, or insufficient permissions, an error MUST NOT be generated. Dangling references are permitted.

review.note: Dangling, unavailable and access-denied bases must not make the authored Message invalid solely because they cannot be resolved. Server admission preserves references through publication/restart without invoking target validation. Consumer callbacks return explicit NotFound/Unavailable/AccessDenied statuses; UnavailableBasesRemainExplicitlyIncompleteWithoutFallback and APartiallyAvailableChainKeepsKnownOverlaysAndReportsItsMissingTail retain known metadata while marking incomplete composition. Unexpected callback failures are not converted into these permitted missing outcomes. Full qualification remains pending.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Definition Registry Model / Message Definitions (Message Group) / `basemessage`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

review.note: Read as basemessage optionality, not permission to skip supplied-reference validation. Base-free definition materialization and schema-only Message admission do not invent a base; supplied local/absolute references retain type/syntax and authorized-acquisition obligations. BaseDefinitionIsDeeplyOverlaidWithoutChangingTheAuthoredIdentity and MessageSchemaRulesAcceptNearestValidDeclarations provide the adjacent behavior evidence. Recursive acquisition and whole-array overlay semantics remain separate.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Definition Registry Model / Message Definitions (Message Group) / `basemessage`

requirements.text: - If the value is a relative reference, it MUST be a valid `xid` of a Resource, or Version, of type `message` as defined by this specification.

review.note: Read with the local-reference paragraph: slash-leading references must identify local Message Resource/Version XIDs, not Registry/Group/Meta/collection/details or request-version targets. requirements.text: - Description: Content type of the message payload. This attribute MAY be duplicative with some other metadata within the message definition. For example, in the case of using CloudEvents, the `envelopemetadata` attribute might include the `datacontenttype` attribute. This possible duplication of data is expected so as to allow for easy, more consistent discovery of the message's format. This means that if this information does appear in more than one location within the message metadata, all occurrences MUST have the same value.

review.note: Read with the following structured-envelope representation exception and case-insensitive media/charset rules. ValidateMessageContentTypes compares concrete declarations on the same representation plane across CloudEvents binary, HTTP/NATS, AMQP, MQTT and Kafka without rewriting authored values. CharsetComparisonAppliesToEachMessageContentTypeDeclaration and CharsetEquivalentContentTypesPublishWithoutRewritingAndInvalidRevisionsRemainAtomic prove cross-surface agreement and atomic mismatch rejection. StructuredEnvelopeKeepsPayloadAndWireContentTypesDistinct separates nested payload from outer wire type. Template constraints retain runtime substitution obligations rather than being treated as concrete equivalent media types.

review.note: Definition materialization maintains payload and representation content types separately. StructuredEnvelopeKeepsPayloadAndWireContentTypesDistinct and StructuredFormatSelectsTheOuterTypeWithoutReplacingTheInferredPayloadType assert the outer CloudEvents format independently of JSON payload inference. requirements.text: As specified in [RFC 2045](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2045), the media type part of the content type MUST be treated in a case-insensitive manner by consumers, along with the attribute names in parameters. For example, a `datacontenttype` of `text/plain; charset=utf-8` MUST be treated in the same way as `TEXT/Plain; CharSet=utf-8`.

review.note: Consumer content-type equivalence uses case-insensitive media type and parameter names. Read with the referenced RFC 2046 section 4.1.2: charset values are also explicitly case-insensitive, unlike general parameter values. RegistryDomainRules.ContentTypes now compares decoded charset values case-insensitively without rewriting metadata; other parameter values remain ordinal after unquoting. ContentTypeCharsetComparisonPreservesOtherParameterSemantics covers mixed case, quoting, order, different/missing charsets, case-sensitive profile/boundary values and existing duplicate-parameter order policy. CharsetComparisonAppliesToEachMessageContentTypeDeclaration covers CloudEvents binary and HTTP/NATS/AMQP/MQTT/Kafka. CharsetEquivalentContentTypesPublishWithoutRewritingAndInvalidRevisionsRemainAtomic covers retained authored values, invalid revisions, event stability and restart. This does not assert charset alias equivalence or arbitrary registered media-type parameter semantics. Full per-requirement qualification remains pending.

source.section: Schema Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: The schema registry therefore allows managing multiple versions of schemas, declares their lineage, and states their compatibility policy. The compatibility policy is used to determine whether a schema change is compatible with prior versions and whether data that has been serialized based on prior versions can still be deserialized and/or validated using the new schema. This compatibility check is important to ensure that changes to schemas do not inadvertently break the ability to read existing data, and MAY be enforced by implementations of the schema registry. The [xRegistry Core][xRegistry Core] specification defines the versioning and compatibility relationship mechanisms.

review.note: Read the complete active upstream-d290b1ec Schema spec and model, including the document-store and lineage examples. Enforcement is optional here, but selected compatibility modes invoke Core obligations. BuiltInRegistryResourceValidator checks actual ancestor Documents, not version-name order; Avro has semantic resolution and other formats only exact-byte proofs. Broad compatibility qualification remains pending, including the separate Core admission conflict; this overview is not whole-format conformance.

However, as with all attributes, if accepting the attribute would result in a bad state (such as exceeding a size limit, or results in a security issue), then the server MAY choose to reject the request.

review.note: The active Schema model admits Group/Version wildcard any data; SchemaWildcardExtensionsRoundTripWithoutRewritingExactValuesOrDocumentBytes checks exact stored extension values and unchanged Document bytes. source.section: Schema Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 2. Notations and Terminology / 2.2. Terminology / 2.2.1. Schema

requirements.text: We use the term **schema** (or schema Resource) in this specification as a logical grouping of **schema Versions**. A **schema Version** is a concrete document. The **schema** Resource is a semantic umbrella formed around one or more concrete schema Version documents that represent iterations of the same logical schema. Per the definition of the [`compatibility`][xRegistry compatibility] attribute, all Versions of a single **schema** MUST adhere to the rules defined by the `compatibility` attribute. Any breaking change MUST result in a new **schema** Resource being created.

review.note: Separate Resource identity and selected compatibility policy are distinct obligations. BreakingSchemaEvolutionRequiresADifferentResourceUnderTheDeclaredPolicy rejects a proven incompatible Avro candidate and publishes it under a new Resource while preserving the original. IncompatibleAvroMutationsPreserveAllVersionsAndPolicy also checks changed ancestors, policies and ancestry. Unknown policies/changed non-Avro schemas are not proven compatibility and remain outside broad qualification; no automatic migration to a new Resource is inferred.

The [`deprecated`][xRegistry deprecated] attribute MAY be used to indicate the appropriate new schema to use following a breaking change.

review.note: Deprecation is optional Core metadata, not a requirement to discover, create or retrieve a replacement Resource. Compatibility evidence is scoped to actual selected policies. A Schema-specific deprecation/replacement lifecycle workflow has not been qualified here; generic deprecation behavior does not establish that workflow.
